title: Lazy ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration
body:
**Expected Behavior**

When using Spring AI MCP client in a Spring Cloud microservice environment, the `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration` should **not require the MCP server to be up at application startup**, and it should be possible to make the tool callback conversion **lazy-initialized**.

Concretely, I would expect:

* The auto-configuration to support a **`lazy` option** (or similar flag) so that the MCP client/tool callback infrastructure can be initialized **on first use**, rather than eagerly during context refresh.
* The application should be able to start even if the MCP server microservice is not running yet, especially in development environments where the MCP server is optional.
* Excluding `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration` should not be the only way to avoid startup-time failures, because doing so also prevents injection of `McpServerFeatures.SyncToolSpecification` and `McpServerFeatures.AsyncToolSpecification`.

For example, a configuration property like this would solve the problem:

```yaml
spring:
  ai:
    mcp:
      tool-callback:
        lazy-init: true  # or similar name
```

With `lazy-init=true`, the MCP client/tool callback conversion should only attempt to connect to the MCP server when a tool is actually invoked, not during application startup.

---

**Current Behavior**

I am using Spring Cloud to call an internal MCP server microservice via a custom `McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer` and `LoadBalancerClient`:

```java
@Bean
public McpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer mcpSyncHttpClientRequestCustomizer(
        LoadBalancerClient loadBalancerClient) {

    return (builder, method, endpoint, body, context) -> {

        ServiceInstance serviceInstance = loadBalancerClient.choose(endpoint.getHost());
        if (serviceInstance == null) {
            return;
        }

        URI newEndpoint = UrlBuilder
                .of(endpoint, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
                .setHost(serviceInstance.getHost())
                .setPort(serviceInstance.getPort())
                .toURI();

        builder.uri(newEndpoint);
    };
}
```

```yaml
spring:
  ai:
    mcp:
      server:
        protocol: sse
        # boot mode add /ai-mcp-server, cloud mode remove it!
        base-url: /ai-mcp-server
        sse-endpoint: /sse
      client:
        # disable initialized
        initialized: false
        sse:
          connections:
            ai-mcp-server:
              url: http://ai-mcp-server
              sse-endpoint: ${spring.ai.mcp.server.sse-endpoint}
```

However, `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration` is **eagerly initialized at startup**.
If the MCP server microservice is not running, the initialization fails and the **entire Spring Boot application fails to start**.

This means:

* When I use Spring Cloud to integrate with an internal MCP server microservice, the client application is effectively **forced** to require the MCP server to be up at startup.
* Even when the MCP server and client are in the **same application**, the eager initialization can still cause startup failures if the MCP endpoint is not yet available.
* In development, MCP is **not mandatory** for all features, but the auto-configuration currently behaves as if it were.

The only way I’ve found to avoid the startup failure is to exclude the auto-configuration:

```java
@SpringBootApplication(exclude = ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration.class)
public class MyApplication {
}
```

But this has a serious drawback: once I exclude `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration`, I **cannot inject** `McpServerFeatures.SyncToolSpecification` and `McpServerFeatures.AsyncToolSpecification` anymore, which I still want to use.

So right now I must choose between:

* Having `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration` active, but being forced to start the MCP server for the app to boot; or
* Excluding it to avoid startup failure, but losing access to `McpServerFeatures.SyncToolSpecification` and `McpServerFeatures.AsyncToolSpecification`.

---

**Context**

* **How has this issue affected you?**
  I am building a microservice architecture where one service acts as an MCP server, and other services act as MCP clients using Spring AI and Spring Cloud LoadBalancer. In such an environment, services do not always start in a fixed order. When `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration` eagerly initializes and expects the MCP server to be reachable at startup, my client service fails to start if that MCP server is not yet running.

* **What are you trying to accomplish?**
  I want to:

  * Use Spring Cloud LoadBalancer to resolve the MCP server microservice dynamically.
  * Allow my client service to start normally even when the MCP server is not running (especially in development or when I’m testing unrelated features).
  * Still be able to inject and use `McpServerFeatures.SyncToolSpecification` and `McpServerFeatures.AsyncToolSpecification`.

* **What other alternatives have you considered?**

  * Completely excluding `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration` via `@SpringBootApplication(exclude = ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration.class)` – this avoids startup failure but removes useful MCP-related beans.
  * Manually guarding MCP calls with try/catch – this does not help with the **startup-time** eager initialization.
  * Starting a dummy MCP server in dev – this adds unnecessary complexity just to satisfy the auto-config.

* **Are you aware of any workarounds?**
  The only workable workaround today is excluding `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration`, but that prevents injection of `McpServerFeatures.SyncToolSpecification` and `McpServerFeatures.AsyncToolSpecification`, which I would still like to use in the same application.

---

**Feature Request Summary**

Please consider:

* Adding a **lazy-init option** (e.g. `spring.ai.mcp.tool-callback.lazy-init=true`) for `ToolCallbackConverterAutoConfiguration`,
  **or**
* Making the MCP tool callback client initialization conditional on explicit configuration (so that it does not eagerly fail when no MCP server is available),
  **while still allowing** injection of `McpServerFeatures.SyncToolSpecification` and `McpServerFeatures.AsyncToolSpecification`.

This would greatly improve the developer experience when integrating Spring AI MCP in Spring Cloud / microservice environments, and would align better with typical Spring Boot auto-configuration patterns where external services are not strictly required at startup unless explicitly configured.

Way back in the start of Spring AI I set the default temperature to 0.7, this was a mistake.  The value should not be set explicitly and the default value of the vendor used.  This only surfaced as an issue when some models did not accept a temperature value of 0.7.   

Update the docs on 'upgrading to 2.0.0.M1' so users are aware that this may change their program's behavior.

title: Add native structured output support for Mistral AI
body:
**Expected Behavior**

Users should be able to use Spring AI's native structured output integration with Mistral AI:

```java
ChatClient.create(mistralChatModel)
    .prompt("Generate a movie review")
    .advisors(AdvisorParams.ENABLE_NATIVE_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT)
    .call()
    .entity(MovieReview.class);
```

This requires `MistralAiChatOptions` to implement `StructuredOutputChatOptions`, similar to `OpenAiChatOptions`.

**Current Behavior**

`MistralAiChatOptions` only implements `ToolCallingChatOptions`:

```java
public class MistralAiChatOptions implements ToolCallingChatOptions { }
```

This prevents native structured output integration. When using `.entity(Class)`, the check in `ChatModelCallAdvisor` fails:

```java
chatClientRequest.prompt().getOptions() instanceof StructuredOutputChatOptions
// → false for MistralAI, falls back to prompt-based instructions
```

Users must manually generate and inject the JSON schema as a workaround.

**Context**

- Mistral AI's API supports structured outputs with JSON schema

title: Spring AI 1.1.1 breaks compatibility with Spring Boot 3.5's default Kotlin version (Kotlin 1.9.x)
body:
**Bug description**
Upgrading from Spring AI 1.1.0 to 1.1.1 introduces this build error:

```
 (-1, -1) Module was compiled with an incompatible version of Kotlin. The binary version of its metadata is 2.2.0, expected version is 1.9.0.
```

It looks like https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/commit/62b32902bb742561287a3112a6a396e012626c92 broke compatibility with Spring Boot 3.5's default Kotlin version (1.9.25).

**Environment**
Spring Boot 3.5.8 with Spring AI 1.1.1.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create a new Spring Boot application on https://start.spring.io using Maven, Kotlin and Spring Boot 3.5.8.
2. Add `spring-ai-bom:1.1.1` to dependency management.
3. Add `spring-ai-client-chat` as a compile dependency.
4. Run `./mvnw verify`.
5. The build fails with this error: `Module was compiled with an incompatible version of Kotlin. The binary version of its metadata is 2.2.0, expected version is 1.9.0.`

**Expected behavior**
I expect the build to complete without errors, like it does with Spring AI 1.1.0.

**Minimal Complete Reproducible example**

I've published a reproducer project here: https://github.com/breun/spring-ai-1.1.1-kotlin-compatibility-issue

title: MCP Client - OpenAiChatModel: extra body doesn't get merged correctly with options when tools are enabled
body:
**Bug description**
Hi all!
In version `1.1.0` there was an issue where the `extra_body` wasn't passed down properly to the LLM requests. 
In version `1.1.1` this works fine if there are no tools enabled, but if there are the merge of the options doesn't propagate the extra body as well.


**Environment**
- Spring AI version `1.1.1`
- Java 21
- vLLM version `0.12.0`

**Steps to reproduce**
- Set the extraBody inside the `OpenAiChatOptions`
- Inside the extra body send, as an example, "enable_reasoning" as false.
- Execute a prompt that has inside a tool execution


**Expected behavior**
The LLM should receive those extra body info and turn off reasoning.

I think the problem might be here:
```
	// Add the tool definitions to the request's tools parameter.
		List<ToolDefinition> toolDefinitions = this.toolCallingManager.resolveToolDefinitions(requestOptions);
		if (!CollectionUtils.isEmpty(toolDefinitions)) {
			request = ModelOptionsUtils.merge(
					OpenAiChatOptions.builder().tools(this.getFunctionTools(toolDefinitions)).build(), request,
					ChatCompletionRequest.class);
		}
```


Thanks!

This problem affected my project to enable thinking with qwen3-max model

title: RelevancyEvaluator prompt template is not up-to-date in the docs
body:
# RelevancyEvaluator prompt template is not up-to-date in the docs
[Spring AI testing](https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/testing.html#_relevancy_evaluator) page provides the prompt template concerning the RelevancyEvaluator;
```
Your task is to evaluate if the response for the query
is in line with the context information provided.

You have two options to answer. Either YES or NO.

Answer YES, if the response for the query
is in line with context information otherwise NO.

Query:
{query}

Response:
{response}

Context:
{context}

Answer:
```
But according to the current [RelevancyEvaluator](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/spring-ai-client-chat/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/chat/evaluation/RelevancyEvaluator.java) class this prompt template is outdated.

Updated prompt template:
```
Your task is to evaluate if the response for the query is in line with the context information provided.

You have two options to answer. Either YES/ NO.

Answer - YES, if the response for the query is in line with context information otherwise NO.

Query:
{query}

Response: 
{response}

Context: 
{context}

Answer:
```
Can this updated prompt template be added to the docs?

comments.author: ranjitm2001
comments.body:
Hi @KallivdH,

I investigated this issue and found that the documentation has already been updated to match the code in commit 144ae1ec9 ("Support custom template in RelevancyEvaluator") from May 18, 2025.

Comparing the current code in `RelevancyEvaluator.java` with the documentation in `testing.adoc`, they are now identical.

The issue might have been caused by viewing a cached or older version of the documentation. The current docs at https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/testing.html#_relevancy_evaluator should reflect the correct prompt template.

This issue can likely be closed as already resolved.

title: Deepseek V3.2 Tool Call: Missing reasoningContent in OpenAiChatModel.createRequest
body:
Hello Spring AI Team,

I am submitting an issue regarding the integration of Deepseek V3.2 via the spring-ai-starter-model-openai dependency, specifically concerning the Tool Calling functionality.

1. Description of the Bug
When using the Deepseek V3.2 model for tool calling, the API requires the subsequent user message (the function call result) to include the model's intermediate "thoughts" or reasoning content in the message payload for the continuation of the conversation.

I followed the Deepseek requirements and prepared the necessary message structure, which includes the function results and the required reasoning content.

However, after checking the source code, I found that the OpenAiChatModel's createRequest method, which prepares the payload for the OpenAiApi.ChatCompletion endpoint, is not correctly forwarding this information.

In OpenAiChatModel.createRequest, when converting an org.springframework.ai.model.ChatRequest.Message to an com.theokanning.openai.completion.chat.ChatCompletionMessage (or its equivalent in the current OpenAI SDK wrapper), the reasoningContent parameter is consistently being passed as null, even if it is present in the Spring AI Message object.

The relevant section in the Spring AI model should look at the user message that follows a tool call and ensure that fields required by compatible models (like Deepseek V3.2) are included. The missing reasoningContent prevents the model from correctly processing the subsequent tool results, causing the conversation to stall or produce incorrect output.

2. Workaround
To resolve this issue and enable Deepseek V3.2 tool calling, I was forced to override the entire OpenAiChatModel.createRequest method to manually include the reasoningContent in the ChatCompletionMessage object being sent to the Deepseek API endpoint.

3. Expected Behavior
The OpenAiChatModel.createRequest method should be updated to properly retrieve and include the reasoningContent from the input Spring AI Message object when constructing the ChatCompletionMessage for the underlying OpenAI API wrapper, ensuring compatibility with models like Deepseek V3.2 that require this field for post-tool-call communication.

title: CitationDocument does not support cache_control for PDF prompt caching
body:
## Problem

`CitationDocument.toContentBlock()` hardcodes `cacheControl` to `null`, making it impossible to use Anthropic's prompt caching with PDF documents:

```java
// CitationDocument.java line ~85
public AnthropicApi.ContentBlock toContentBlock() {
    AnthropicApi.ContentBlock.Source source = createSource();
    return new AnthropicApi.ContentBlock(source, this.title, 
        this.context, this.citationsEnabled, null);  // <-- null = no cache control
}
```

This means `AnthropicChatOptions.cacheOptions()` with `SYSTEM_AND_TOOLS` strategy has no effect on PDF documents - they are sent uncached on every request.

## Impact

For multi-turn conversations or batch Q&A against a PDF:
- **Without caching:** Each request pays full price for the PDF (~100k+ tokens for a 20-page doc)
- **With caching:** First request caches, subsequent requests get 90% discount

In our test suite (30 questions against a 19-page PDF), this caused ~$11 in API costs instead of ~$1.

## Expected Behavior

`CitationDocument.Builder` should support setting cache control:

```java
CitationDocument doc = CitationDocument.builder()
    .pdf(pdfBytes)
    .title("My Document")
    .citationsEnabled(true)
    .cacheControl(new CacheControl("ephemeral"))  // <-- Add this
    .build();
```

And `toContentBlock()` should pass it through:

```java
public AnthropicApi.ContentBlock toContentBlock() {
    AnthropicApi.ContentBlock.Source source = createSource();
    return new AnthropicApi.ContentBlock(source, this.title, 
        this.context, this.citationsEnabled, this.cacheControl);  // <-- Use field
}
```

## Workaround

Currently the only workaround is to bypass Spring AI and use the Anthropic Java SDK directly with manual `cache_control` on the document content block.

## Environment

- Spring AI: 2.0.0-M1
- Java: 25
- Anthropic model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514

## Related

- #4325 (message-type aware caching) addresses chat messages but not CitationDocument
- Anthropic docs on [prompt caching with citations](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching): "cache the top-level document content blocks that serve as the source material for citations"

title: Confusing WARN log while AWS region resolving
body:
**Bug description**
[Current documentation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/bedrock.html#_connect_to_aws_bedrock) states:

> AWS region is resolved in the following order:
> - Spring-AI Bedrock spring.ai.bedrock.aws.region property.
> - Java System Properties - aws.region.
> - Environment Variables - AWS_REGION.
> - Credential profiles file at the default location (~/.aws/credentials) shared by all AWS SDKs and the AWS CLI.
> - Instance profile region delivered through the Amazon EC2 metadata service.

In case when region configuration provided only using **spring.ai.bedrock.aws.region** property (no Java System Properties, Env Vars, etc) Folowing WARN log appears:
```
o.s.a.b.c.BedrockProxyChatModel - Failed to load region from DefaultAwsRegionProviderChain, using US_EAST_1
2025-12-16T14:51:07.757422240Z software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkClientException: Unable to load region from any of the providers in the chain software.amazon.awssdk.regions.providers.DefaultAwsRegionProviderChain@f989d46: [software.amazon.awssdk.regions.providers.SystemSettingsRegionProvider@1dca91d6: Unable to load region from system settings. Region must be specified either via environment variable (AWS_REGION) or  system property (aws.region)., software.amazon.awssdk.regions.providers.AwsProfileRegionProvider@4ebbee76: No region provided in profile: default, software.amazon.awssdk.regions.providers.InstanceProfileRegionProvider@1c7385d: Unable to contact EC2 metadata service.]
```
It happens in **BedrockConverseProxyChatAutoConfiguration** while [BedrockProxyChatModel.builder()](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/auto-configurations/models/spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-bedrock-ai/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/model/bedrock/converse/autoconfigure/BedrockConverseProxyChatAutoConfiguration.java#L74C19-L74C50) execution. Builder in its constructor [checks DefaultAwsRegionProviderChain](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/models/spring-ai-bedrock-converse/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/bedrock/converse/BedrockProxyChatModel.java#L892-L899) in order to find region and produces WARN log if nothing was found without consideration of **spring.ai.bedrock.aws.region** property. 

Hopefully autoconfiguration [provides region to the builder after creation](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/auto-configurations/models/spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-bedrock-ai/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/model/bedrock/converse/autoconfigure/BedrockConverseProxyChatAutoConfiguration.java#L76), so the resulting ChatModel will use configured region, but WARN log doe's not represent current state of the application and looks confusing.

**Environment**
Spring AI version: 1.1.2

**Expected behavior**
No WARN logs in case **spring.ai.bedrock.aws.region** property exists.

comments.author: garethjevans
comments.body: We've had instances of this where this call to determine the region appears to take up to 7 seconds.  It would be great if we could disable it somehow

comments.author: chelis
comments.body:
Adding context to Gareth's comment.

We can see that [org.springframework.ai.bedrock.converse.BedrockProxyChatModel's Builder class](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/21c38342853d2d881c510ab2f9723302dae81ad9/models/spring-ai-bedrock-converse/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/bedrock/converse/BedrockProxyChatModel.java#L894) tries to determine the region in it's constructor before defaulting to `us_east_1` and before calling code can make use the builder's `region` method to set it. It does this using `DefaultAwsRegionProviderChain` which may end up making a n[etwork call to EC2 Metadata](https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-java/blob/d866126817fcc10595a3e7cd4b40efe626f05a7c/aws-java-sdk-core/src/main/java/com/amazonaws/regions/DefaultAwsRegionProviderChain.java#L26C19-L26C49) endpoint if the region is not set in env variables/config files. 
Being that there is a method provided in the builder to set region, incurring in such penalty if it is not configured globally makes no sense. That region resolution should not be attempted in the constructor, but in the `build()` method if none was provided, or not executed at all.

title: Allow accessing "timestamp" field from spring_ai_chat_memory table programatically when using JdbcChatMemoryRepository
body:
**Expected Behavior**

The timestamp should be accessible programmatically, like any other column in the chat memory table.

**Current Behavior**

When using JdbcChatMemoryRepository, all the details stored in the table `spring_ai_chat_memory` for every chat are accessible via the `Message` object, except for the `timestamp` column. This restricts UI/Chatbot-based applications from displaying the actual timestamp of every chat message. It also restricts one to sort old messages chronologically in any order. Another problem is the implementation of a standard data retention policy for chats.

It forces one to manually maintain another metadata table, causing unnecessary performance overhead and complexity.

**Root Cause Analysis**
I think the issue is in `Neo4jVectorStore.doAdd()` method. The code creates a session using this.driver.session() without passing the configured SessionConfig. My question is, why isn't `sessionConfig` used here? Instead, it using the default configuration. Is there a specific design consideration behind this?

```java
public void doAdd(List<Document> documents) {
        List<float[]> embeddings = this.embeddingModel.embed(documents, EmbeddingOptions.builder().build(), this.batchingStrategy);
        List<Map<String, Object>> rows = documents.stream().map((document) -> {
            return this.documentToRecord(document, (float[])embeddings.get(documents.indexOf(document)));
        }).toList();

        // I think maybe issus is here
        Session session = this.driver.session();

        try {
            String statement = "\tUNWIND $rows AS row\n\tMERGE (u:%s {%2$s: row.id})\n\t\tSET u += row.properties\n\tWITH row, u\n\tCALL db.create.setNodeVectorProperty(u, $embeddingProperty, row[$embeddingProperty])\n".formatted(new Object[]{this.label, this.idProperty});
            session.executeWrite((tx) -> {
                return tx.run(statement, Map.of("rows", rows, "embeddingProperty", this.embeddingProperty)).consume();
            });
        } catch (Throwable var8) {
            if (session != null) {
                try {
                    session.close();
                } catch (Throwable var7) {
                    var8.addSuppressed(var7);
                }
            }

            throw var8;
        }

        if (session != null) {
            session.close();
        }

    }
```

- Spring AI Version: 1.1.2

title: PgVectorStore throws IllegalStateException on validateSchema when table doesn't exist before initialization

comments.author: quaff
comments.body: If you set `initializeSchema=true`, then you shouldn't set `schemaValidation=true`.

comments.author: sdudzin
comments.body:
I opened a PR for this: #6438 

The root cause for the problem is that `PgVectorStore.afterPropertiesSet()` validated the table schema before the schema initialization could create the table, so with both `schemaValidation` and `initializeSchema` enabled the first startup against a fresh database failed. The PR splits validation into two phases: the schema and table names are still validated before any SQL runs (keeping the SQL injection guard), while the table structure is validated after initialization. The validate-only mode (`initializeSchema=false`) is unchanged.

title: [Redis] SemanticCacheAdvisor: Streaming collects all chunks before returning to user
[Redis] `SemanticCacheAdvisor`: Cache key only considers user text, ignores system prompt and context
body:
The cache key is derived only from the user's message text, ignoring system prompts, conversation history, and model parameters.

  ## Current Behavior
  ```java
  private String extractUserTextFromRequest(ChatClientRequest request) {
      return request.prompt().getUserMessage().getText();
  }
```

 ## Problem

  Two identical questions with different system prompts will hit the same cache entry:

  - Query: "Summarize this" + System: "You are a technical writer" → Response A
  - Query: "Summarize this" + System: "You are a poet" → Returns Response A (incorrect!)

  Similarly, different model parameters (temperature, etc.) are not considered.

  ## Suggested Approach

  Consider including in the cache key:
  1. System prompt (or its hash)
  2. Relevant model parameters (temperature, model name)
  3. Optionally, conversation history context

title: [Redis] `DefaultSemanticCache`: Gson serialization loses token usage, finish reason, and tool calls
body:
The custom `ChatResponseAdapter` for Gson serialization only preserves text content and basic generation structure, losing important metadata.

  ## Lost Information
  - Token usage (prompt tokens, completion tokens)
  - Finish reason
  - Model metadata
  - Tool calls and function results

  ## Current Behavior
  The `ChatResponseAdapter` serializes a simplified version of the response.

  ## Impact
  Applications relying on token usage for billing/monitoring or finish reason for flow control will get incorrect/missing data from cached responses.

  ## Suggested Approach
  1. Serialize the complete `ChatResponse` structure
  2. Or document this as a known limitation
  3. Consider using a more complete serialization strategy

comments.author: sobychacko
comments.body:
After further review, we've decided to defer this issue. The core semantic caching functionality -- caching and retrieving LLM text responses based on semantic similarity -- is complete and working as intended.

The metadata being lost (token usage, model name, finish reason) is secondary to the primary use case. We'll address these improvements if there is sufficient user demand.

title: Migrate MongoDB Atlas container support to the new native feature in Spring Boot 4
body:
Currently, Spring AI defines a series of `ContainerConnectionDetailsFactory` to support Testcontainers with several vector stores and inference services. One of them is [`MongoDbAtlasLocalContainerConnectionDetailsFactory`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/spring-ai-spring-boot-testcontainers/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/testcontainers/service/connection/mongo/MongoDbAtlasLocalContainerConnectionDetailsFactory.java).

As of Spring Boot 4, there is a native [`MongoDbAtlasLocalContainerConnectionDetailsFactory`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/module/spring-boot-mongodb/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/mongodb/testcontainers/MongoDbAtlasLocalContainerConnectionDetailsFactory.java) directly in the Spring MongoDB module. 

For Spring AI 2.0, I recommend migrating to the native support in Spring Boot. Otherwise, if an application is using MongoDB Atlas both from Spring Data and Spring AI Vector Store, two different configurations will be needed.

title: Add support for Google GenAI Image Generation (Gemini) in Spring AI
body:
Please do a quick search on GitHub issues first, the feature you are about to request might have already been requested.

# Add support for Google GenAI Image Generation (Gemini) in Spring AI

## Expected Behavior

Spring AI should provide first-class support for Google GenAI (Gemini) image generation models (`gemini-2.5-flash-image`, `gemini-3-pro-image-preview`, etc.) as a model type, similar to existing support for text and embeddings. Ideally support should include:

- A new `ImageModel` implementation for Gemini image generation
- A Spring Boot starter and auto-configuration
- Mapping Gemini image responses into `ImageResponse`
- A prompt abstraction supporting:
  - text instructions
  - inline base64 images
  - aspect ratio / resolution parameters
- Configuration properties for defaults

**Example (illustrative):**

```java
GoogleGenAiImagePrompt prompt = GoogleGenAiImagePrompt.builder()
    .text("Add happy pug to the picture of the man.")
    .addImage(existingBase64Image, "image/jpeg")
    .build();

ImageResponse images = imageModel.call(prompt);
```


## Current Behavior

Spring AI currently supports Google GenAI for:

- Chat (text)
- Embeddings

but **not** for image generation. Developers must call the Google GenAI Java SDK directly, bypassing Spring AI abstractions. There is no unified integration with:

- `ImageModel`
- `ImagePrompt`
- `ImageResponse`
- Spring Boot configuration properties

## Context

I am building a Spring Boot application that uses Gemini image generation. While the GenAI Java SDK works directly, an official Spring AI integration would:

- improve DX
- align with existing `ImageModel` implementations
- support multimodal Gemini use cases
- leverage Spring Boot starters and configuration

There are no reasonable workarounds that reuse Spring AI abstractions without reimplementing core pieces of the framework.

I am willing to contribute a PR. I already have a working implementation of:

- `GoogleGenAiImageModel`
- `GoogleGenAiImageApi` (low-level SDK adapter)
- `GoogleGenAiImageOptions`
- Spring Boot auto-configuration
- unit tests

title: MongoChatMemoryRepository is changing the order of the messages to descending during fetch and consequently the LLM is behaving unexpectedly

comments.author: chanani
comments.body:
Hi @tinomthomas,

I'd like to work on this issue if it's still available.

## Problem Analysis

The bug is in `MongoChatMemoryRepository.findByConversationId()` where messages are sorted in **descending order** (`Sort.by("timestamp").descending()`), while the PostgreSQL implementation uses **ascending order** (implicit in `ORDER BY "timestamp"`).

This causes the conversation history to be reversed (ASSISTANT, USER, ASSISTANT, USER...), which confuses the LLM as it expects chronological order.

## Proposed Solution

Change the sort order from descending to ascending:
```java
@Override
public List<Message> findByConversationId(String conversationId) {
    var messages = this.mongoTemplate.query(Conversation.class)
        .matching(Query.query(Criteria.where("conversationId").is(conversationId))
            .with(Sort.by("timestamp").ascending())); // Change to ascending
    return messages.stream()
        .map(MongoChatMemoryRepository::mapMessage)
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
}
```

## Testing Plan

1. Add/update integration tests to verify message ordering
2. Ensure compatibility with existing MongoDB-based chat memory functionality
3. Verify that messages are returned in chronological order (USER → ASSISTANT → USER → ASSISTANT...)

I'll follow the DCO process and sign off my commits. Please let me know if I can proceed with this fix.

Thanks!

comments.body:
@chanani Sure.Please go ahead.

Also, I would love to know the opinion of @deejay1 (original author of this implementation). He might had some other rationale in mind during the implementation.

title: Unable to configure HTTP connect/read timeouts via configuration properties
body:
Bug description
It is currently not possible to configure HTTP connection and read timeouts for interacting with Large Language Models (LLMs) via Spring Boot configuration properties (e.g., in application.properties or application.yml).

Users have to manually define a RestClient or WebClient bean to customize these timeouts, which defeats the purpose of the auto-configuration provided by the Spring AI starters. Relying on the default HTTP client timeouts is often not suitable for production environments where network stability varies.

Environment

Spring AI version: 1.1.2
Java version: 17
OS: Windows / Linux / macOS
Starter used: spring-ai-openai-spring-boot-starter 
Steps to reproduce

Create a Spring Boot project and include spring-ai-openai-spring-boot-starter.
Configure the API key in application.yml:
```
yaml


spring:
  ai:
    openai:
      api-key: sk-...
      # Attempt to set timeouts here 
      chat:
        options:
          connect-timeout: 5s
          read-timeout: 30s
```
Run a simple chat completion request.
Observe that the connection/read timeouts used are the default HTTP client timeouts , not the values intended in the configuration.
Expected behavior
The Spring AI starters should expose configuration properties to allow users to easily override the default HTTP client timeouts.

Ideally, properties similar to these should be supported:
```

yaml


spring:
  ai:
    openai: # or anthropic, azure, etc.
      base-url: ...
      api-key: ...
      client:
        connect-timeout: 5s
        read-timeout: 60s
```
This would allow the auto-configuration to build the underlying RestClient (or WebClient) with the specified timeouts without requiring manual Bean definitions.

comments.author: ilayaperumalg
comments.body:
Hi @hbsjz-swl, Thanks for reporting! Currently, We expect the HTTP client configuration options provided explicitly via RESTClient and WebClient builders which you can override. There are some discussions related to this in these: 

https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/issues/512
https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/pull/4970 
https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/pull/2808

Closing this issue for now and we can track from #512

title: Support for reasoning_content field in OpenAI-compatible models Kimi during Tool Calling
body: According to the API specifications of Moonshot Kimi 2.5K, if thinking is enabled, the subsequent message in the conversation history must include the reasoning_content (even if empty) in the Assistant message. Currently, Spring AI's message mapping logic seems to drop this field, leading to the following error when the tool result is sent back to the model: "thinking is enabled but reasoning_content is missing in assistant tool call message at index X"

title: Refactor Model|ChatOptions handling
body:
The current logic for handling `ChatOptions` merging between default and per-prompt options is very cumbersome and error-prone. It relies on the options classes being Jackson annotated, even though options have no point being serialized on the wire (directly).
Moreover, this behavior conflicts with easily stating which fields are required and which fields are not, because the current logic deals with half-populated objects (the per-prompt overrides).

This issue is about refactoring this from the ground up, with the following plan:
* Option classes can clearly state which fields are required or not. Valid construction is enforced by a Builder.
* Builders are used as a vehicle for stating options overrides, as they allow partial definition of state
* `ModelOptionsUtils.merge()` and similar methods become irrelevant

comments.author: nicolaskrier
comments.body:
`ChatOptions` are also used as nested configuration property (see [`OllamaChatProperties`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/auto-configurations/models/spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-ollama/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/model/ollama/autoconfigure/OllamaChatProperties.java) for example) and all the conversions between string and the different properties types should be handled to be configurable in properties files (see #4854).

It is a bit out of context here but it is yet another conversion that has to be done correctly.

title: MetadataMode is ignored in batched embedding path used by vector stores
body:
**Bug description**

The [`EmbeddingModel`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/spring-ai-model/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/embedding/EmbeddingModel.java#L92) interface's default `embed(List<Document>, EmbeddingOptions, BatchingStrategy)` method extracts text via `Document::getText`, completely ignoring the `MetadataMode` configured on the embedding model. This means that when vector stores call this batched embedding path (which all built-in vector stores do), metadata is never included in the embedding text, regardless of the `MetadataMode` configuration.

There is an inconsistency between the single-document and batched embedding paths:

- `OpenAiEmbeddingModel.embed(Document)` correctly uses `document.getFormattedContent(this.metadataMode)`.
- `EmbeddingModel.embed(List<Document>, EmbeddingOptions, BatchingStrategy)` uses `Document::getText`, ignoring `metadataMode` entirely.

Since all built-in vector stores (e.g., `PgVectorStore.doAdd()`) call the batched path, the `MetadataMode` parameter accepted by embedding model constructors (e.g., `new OpenAiEmbeddingModel(api, MetadataMode.EMBED, options)`) is effectively dead code when used with vector stores.

Additionally, the `TokenCountBatchingStrategy` accepts a `ContentFormatter` and `MetadataMode`, but only uses them for **token counting** to size sub-batches -- not for formatting the actual text sent to the embedding API. This creates a misleading API surface: users may configure `MetadataMode.EMBED` expecting metadata to be included in embeddings, but it is silently ignored.

**Environment**

- Spring AI version: 2.0.0-M2 (also reproducible on `main` branch at time of writing)
- Java version: 25
- Vector store: PgVectorStore (but applies to all vector stores using the default `EmbeddingModel.embed(documents, options, batchingStrategy)`)

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create an `OpenAiEmbeddingModel` with `MetadataMode.EMBED`:
   ```java
   var embeddingModel = new OpenAiEmbeddingModel(openAiApi, MetadataMode.EMBED, options);
   ```

2. Create a `PgVectorStore` (or any vector store) with this embedding model:
   ```java
   var vectorStore = PgVectorStore.builder(jdbcTemplate, embeddingModel)
       .batchingStrategy(new TokenCountBatchingStrategy(
           EncodingType.CL100K_BASE, 8191, 0.1,
           DefaultContentFormatter.defaultConfig(),
           MetadataMode.EMBED))
       .build();
   ```

3. Add a document with metadata:
   ```java
   vectorStore.add(List.of(
       new Document("Some content", Map.of("title", "Getting Started", "tags", "tutorial"))
   ));
   ```

4. Observe that the text sent to the embedding API is only `"Some content"` -- the metadata fields `title` and `tags` are not included, despite `MetadataMode.EMBED` being configured in both the embedding model and the batching strategy.

**Expected behavior**

When `MetadataMode.EMBED` is configured, the batched embedding path should use `Document.getFormattedContent(metadataMode)` (or equivalent) so that metadata is included in the text sent to the embedding API, consistent with the single-document `embed(Document)` path.

**Minimal Complete Reproducible example**

The issue is in the default method of `EmbeddingModel.java`:

```java
// EmbeddingModel.java (default method)
default List<float[]> embed(List<Document> documents, @Nullable EmbeddingOptions options,
        BatchingStrategy batchingStrategy) {
    // ...
    for (List<Document> subBatch : batch) {
        List<String> texts = subBatch.stream().map(Document::getText).toList(); // BUG: should use getFormattedContent
        EmbeddingRequest request = new EmbeddingRequest(texts, options);
        // ...
    }
    return embeddings;
}
```

Compare with `OpenAiEmbeddingModel.embed(Document)`:

```java
// OpenAiEmbeddingModel.java
@Override
public float[] embed(Document document) {
    return this.embed(document.getFormattedContent(this.metadataMode)); // CORRECT: uses formatted content
}
```

A possible fix would be to propagate the `MetadataMode` into the batched path, either by:
1. Adding a `MetadataMode` parameter to the `embed(documents, options, batchingStrategy)` method, or
2. Having the default implementation delegate to `embed(Document)` per document (though this loses batching benefits), or
3. Adding a `metadataMode` accessor to the `EmbeddingModel` interface that the default method can use.

title: gen_ai.client.token.usage Missing in Spring Boot 4
body:
When I upgrade to Spring Boot 4, I no longer get the `gen_ai.client.token.usage` actuator metric.

Tested with Spring AI `1.1.2` and `2.0.0-M2` and with the Bedrock Converse & OpenAI SDK chat clients.

comments.author: sobychacko
comments.body:
@jamesward I think this is whats causing this issue. In Spring Boot 3.x, the `ObservationAutoConfiguration` class lived at `org.springframework.boot.actuate.autoconfigure.observation.ObservationAutoConfiguration` and declared an
  explicit ordering dependency `(after = CompositeMeterRegistryAutoConfiguration)`, which guaranteed that a `MeterRegistry` bean was available by the time it ran.

  Spring AI's observation auto-configurations (for chat, embedding, image, and vector store) used `@AutoConfiguration(afterName =
  "org.springframework.boot.actuate.autoconfigure.observation.ObservationAutoConfiguration")` to ensure they processed after Boot's observation setup, which transitively ensured `MeterRegistry` was present. In Spring Boot 4, this class was moved to `org.springframework.boot.micrometer.observation.autoconfigure.ObservationAutoConfiguration` as part of the actuator module restructuring. The old class no longer exists. When Spring Boot's `AutoConfigurationSorter` encounters an `afterName` reference to a non-existent class, it silently drops the ordering constraint. This means Spring AI's observation auto-configurations can now process before the metrics auto-configurations have created a `MeterRegistry` bean. When that happens, the `@ConditionalOnBean(MeterRegistry.class)` condition on `ChatModelMeterObservationHandler` (and similar handler beans) evaluates to `false`, and the handler bean is never created. Without this handler, no `gen_ai.client.token.usage` counter metrics are ever generated.

  We need to update the `afterName` references in all affected auto-configuration classes to point to the Boot 4 class locations:

```  
@AutoConfiguration(afterName = {
      "org.springframework.boot.micrometer.observation.autoconfigure.ObservationAutoConfiguration",
      "org.springframework.boot.micrometer.metrics.autoconfigure.CompositeMeterRegistryAutoConfiguration" })
```

The second entry is the key one — it ensures the auto-configuration runs after `CompositeMeterRegistryAutoConfiguration`, which is where the `MeterRegistry` bean is created. The first entry preserves the original semantic intent of running after the observation infrastructure is set up.

PR created here: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/pull/5472

comments.author: jamesward
comments.body: Nice! Amazing work sleuthing that out. Thank you!

title: Bedrock Structured Output
body:
Some models on Bedrock now support native structured output:
https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/02/structured-outputs-available-amazon-bedrock/

Please add support in `AdvisorParams.ENABLE_NATIVE_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT` for this.

comments.author: tzolov
comments.body:
Thanks for sharing this @jamesward 

To add native SO support to a ChatModel, you only need to extend its ChatOptions to implement the `StructuredOutputChatOptions` interface. 

For reference: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/ac9254fa55085115274ce981de226519181845aa/models/spring-ai-openai-sdk/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/openaisdk/OpenAiSdkChatOptions.java#L47

comments.author: chanani
comments.body:
Hi @jamesward @tzolov ! I've started working on this issue and submitted a PR that implements `StructuredOutputChatOptions` in `BedrockChatOptions`.

### What was done
- `BedrockChatOptions` now implements `StructuredOutputChatOptions`
- Added `outputSchema` field with getter/setter and Builder support
- Added unit tests

### Current limitation
The current AWS SDK version (2.36.3) used by Spring AI does not include the `OutputConfig` class for the Converse API yet. So the output schema is stored as a plain `String` field for now, consistent with how other providers like Google GenAI handle it.

Once the AWS SDK dependency is upgraded to a version that includes `OutputConfig`, `BedrockProxyChatModel` can be updated to pass the schema to the Converse API via `outputConfig.textFormat`.

title: Make `ToolCallAdvisor` the default tool call management option
body:
Currently, the tool-call lifecycle is managed internally by each concrete ChatModel implementation. 

The ToolCallAdvisor allows you to manage this lifecycle as a part of the Advisor chains. The latter provides clear visibility for the tool request and response messages, allowing manipulation and storing of those messages in Memory. This is a requirement for many AI and Agentic use cases.

When the ToolCallAdvisor is added to the chain (e.g. ChatClient.advisors(ToolCallAdsvior.builder()...), it disables the low-level ChatMemory tool handling implementations. The proposal is to auto-register the ToolCallAdvisor by default when there are registered ChatClient Tools or tool callbacks.

Also a the toolcall advisor should disable its internal conversation memory support if there are ChatMemory advisors registered after it in the chain.

comments.author: aks151
comments.body: Hi @tzolov can i pick it up?

comments.author: bkoragan
comments.body:
@tzolov @sdeleuze 
I was triaging #5792, which reports that when streamToolCallResponses(true) is enabled on ToolCallAdvisor, the AssistantMessage with tool call requests is emitted in the Flux, but the corresponding ToolResponseMessage (the tool's actual result) is consumed internally and never surfaced to the consumer.

This issue aligns with my observations. Both stem from the same root: the tool-call lifecycle is not fully transparent to consumers. #5792 is the symptom (incomplete streaming output), and this is more of the architectural fix (making ToolCallAdvisor first-class so the full lifecycle is visible through the advisor chain).

**I'd like to propose the following solution:**

1. Auto-register ToolCallAdvisor when tools are present: 
when tools or tool callbacks are registered on ChatClient, auto-register ToolCallAdvisor into the advisor chain that making the advisor chain the single path for tool-call handling & removing the hidden model level loop.. If a user explicitly provides their own ToolCallAdvisor (e.g. with custom streamToolCallResponses or ToolCallingManager settings), skip the auto-registration to respect their configuration.

2. Disable internal conversation memory when a ChatMemory advisor follows:
Auto-detect if a ChatMemory advisor is registered after ToolCallAdvisor in the chain, and if so, disable conversationHistoryEnabled to avoid duplication or conflicts in conversation history management.

3. Emit ToolResponseMessage in the stream (addresses this #5792):
when streamToolCallResponses = true, emit a synthetic ChatClientResponse containing the ToolResponseMessage into the Flux right after tool execution. so consumers see the complete round-trip: tool call request > tool response > model's final result/answer. This is gated behind the existing flag, so default behavior stays unchanged.

If this direction looks good, I'd be happy to open a PR for it.

comments.author: weijiafu14
comments.body:
This is a known Gemini API constraint: when thinking mode is enabled, parts **with** `thoughtSignature` and parts **without** it cannot coexist in the same message. The fix is to split the assistant message into two:

1. First message: text parts (no signature)
2. Second message: functionCall parts (with signature)

Reference: [Gemini thought signature docs](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures) — "Don't merge one part with a signature with another part without a signature"

I've fixed the same bug in LiteLLM ([PR #23809](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/23809)) and documented the full solution in [gemini-claude-bridge](https://github.com/weijiafu14/gemini-claude-bridge) — see [`_split_mixed_model_messages()`](https://github.com/weijiafu14/gemini-claude-bridge/blob/main/src/gemini_claude_bridge/request_converter.py) for the splitting logic.

For Spring AI, the equivalent fix would be in the Google GenAI chat model's message builder, splitting the `Content` when it contains both text `Part`s and `FunctionCall` `Part`s with `thoughtSignature`.

title: Neo4jVectorstore: Make filterExpressionConverter configurable via builder in Neo4jVectorStore
body:
## Summary

The `filterExpressionConverter` field in `Neo4jVectorStore` is currently hardcoded as a final field initialized inline, making it impossible to customize filter expression conversion behavior without subclassing the store itself.

## Current Behavior
```java
private final Neo4jVectorFilterExpressionConverter filterExpressionConverter = new Neo4jVectorFilterExpressionConverter();
```

There is no way to override this converter through the builder, even though the builder pattern is used for all other configuration.

## Desired Behavior

The builder should expose a `filterExpressionConverter(...)` method accepting a `FilterExpressionConverter`, allowing users to plug in a custom implementation:
```java
Neo4jVectorStore vectorStore = Neo4jVectorStore.builder(driver, embeddingModel)
    .filterExpressionConverter(new MyCustomFilterExpressionConverter())
    .build();
```

## Proposed Changes

- Add a `filterExpressionConverter` field to `Neo4jVectorStore.Builder` defaulting to `new Neo4jVectorFilterExpressionConverter()`
- Add a `filterExpressionConverter(FilterExpressionConverter)` setter on the builder
- Change the field type in `Neo4jVectorStore` from `Neo4jVectorFilterExpressionConverter` to `FilterExpressionConverter` to keep the extension point open
- Initialize the field from the builder in the constructor

## Motivation

Users with custom metadata structures or Neo4j-specific query requirements may need to adapt filter expression conversion without forking the class. Using the `FilterExpressionConverter` interface rather than the concrete class also aligns with the open/closed principle and is consistent with how other extension points in Spring AI are designed.

title: Can't attach XLSX file to Amazon Bedrock Converse prompt
body:
### **Bug description**

When I want to add Media (`org.springframework.ai.content.Media#Media(org.springframework.util.MimeType, org.springframework.core.io.Resource)`) to the UserMessage with XLSX file and use this message in Amazon Bedrock Converse API call (Claude Opus), I've get this runtime error:
```
software.amazon.awssdk.services.bedrockruntime.model.ValidationException: The document file name can only contain alphanumeric characters, whitespace characters, hyphens, parentheses, and square brackets. The name can't contain more than one consecutive whitespace character. Check that the file name conforms to these restrictions and retry your request. 
```

The problem is that mime type of this file is `vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet` and when I'm using `Media` class constructor that take `MimeType` and `Resource` (`UrlResource` in my case) then the name of this object is created as follows:

```
this.name = generateDefaultName(mimeType);
```
generateDefaultName (https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/628b020041f94fb223ffd873e94c9304c42bc10f/spring-ai-commons/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/content/Media.java#L161) :

```
private static String generateDefaultName(MimeType mimeType) {
		return NAME_PREFIX + mimeType.getSubtype() + "-" + java.util.UUID.randomUUID();
	}
```
This name is passed to Amazon Bedrock and dots are causing runtime exception. 


### **Environment**

1.0.2 but the newest version is also affected

### **Steps to reproduce**

Described in description. 

### **Expected behavior**

The name should be stripped from dots when passed to Amazon Bedrock converse call. 

**Minimal Complete Reproducible example**

1. Use Amazon Bedrock ChatClient:
```
 val options = BedrockChatOptions.builder()
            .model("eu.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1")
            .build()

        val chatModel = bedrockModelBuilder()
            .asyncReadTimeout(ofSeconds(120))
            .socketTimeout(ofSeconds(120))
            .connectionTimeout(ofSeconds(120))
            .connectionAcquisitionTimeout(ofSeconds(20))
            .defaultOptions(options)
            .build()
        return ChatClient.builder(chatModel).defaultAdvisors(memory).build()
```
2.  Create `UserMessage` with at least one `Media` of XLSX and `Prompt` object:
```
            Media(MimeType.valueOf("application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet"), UrlResource(signedUrl.url))
```

3.  Call using chatClient:
```
chatClient.prompt(prompt)
                .call()
                .entity(clazz)
```
### **Workaround**
You can use `Media.builder()` and then you can pass name excplictly :

```
 val mimeType = MimeType.valueOf(contentType)
 Media.builder()
     .mimeType(mimeType)
     .data(UrlResource(url))
     .name("media-${mimeType.subtype.replace(".", "-")}-${UUID.randomUUID()}")
     .build()
```

title: Anthropic: support multi-block system messages with independent cache_control per block
body:
**Expected Behavior**

Developers should be able to designate portions of the system message as static (cacheable) vs dynamic (uncacheable), with `buildSystemContent()` emitting separate Anthropic `ContentBlock`s accordingly:

```json
{
  "system": [
    {"type": "text", "text": "static instructions...", "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}},
    {"type": "text", "text": "dynamic per-request context..."}
  ]
}
```

Anthropic's API already supports arrays of content blocks in the `system` field, each with independent `cache_control` (up to 4 breakpoints per request). The static block would get cache hits on subsequent requests while the dynamic block is processed fresh.

One possible API shape — a cache policy on `SystemMessage`:

```java
// Static behavioral instructions — cached
new SystemMessage("safety guardrails...", CachePolicy.CACHEABLE);

// Dynamic advisor-injected context — not cached
new SystemMessage("product recommendations...", CachePolicy.NO_CACHE);
```

Another option would be at the advisor level, letting advisors declare whether their `augmentSystemMessage()` output belongs in a cached or uncached block.

**Current Behavior**

`AnthropicChatModel.buildSystemContent()` concatenates all system messages into a single string via `Collectors.joining()`, then wraps the result in one `ContentBlock` with one `cache_control` marker.

This means if *any* part of the system message is dynamic, the entire system cache misses every request. With `SYSTEM_ONLY` strategy enabled, each miss pays Anthropic's 1.25x cache-write cost with zero reads — making it **more expensive** than disabling caching entirely.

There is no way to split static from dynamic content within the system message using the current API. The only workaround is moving dynamic content out of the system message entirely.

**Context**

Our application uses Anthropic Sonnet for conversational AI agents. The system message has two layers:

- **Static behavioral instructions** (~2,280 tokens): safety guardrails, domain principles, brand tone, mode instructions, response formatting. Identical across all requests for a given tenant + mode.
- **Dynamic context injected by Spring AI advisors**: RAG-matched product recommendations (change every query), intent/slot state (change every turn), temporal context (changes daily).

Because `buildSystemContent()` concatenates everything into one block, we can't cache the static prefix independently. Enabling `SYSTEM_ONLY` with any dynamic advisor content means 100% cache misses at 1.25x write cost.

**Workaround:** We moved all dynamic content from the system message to the user message, keeping the system message fully static and cacheable. This works — cache reads cost 0.1x ($0.30/MTok vs $3/MTok uncached for Sonnet) — but it conflates the semantic distinction between system instructions (developer authority) and user-level context. Product recommendations and intent state are contextual data the model *reads*, not behavioral instructions it *follows*, so the practical impact is minimal. But ideally the framework wouldn't force this trade-off.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Bypassing Spring AI to call the Anthropic API directly with fine-grained block placement — loses the entire advisor pipeline
- Waiting for multi-block support — filed this issue

**Related:** #4325 (per-message-type TTLs and min-size thresholds) is complementary but doesn't address static/dynamic splitting within system messages.

**References:**
- [Anthropic Prompt Caching docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) — multi-block system message examples
- Spring AI version: 1.1.0

comments.author: sobychacko
comments.body:
@CalamityAdam Thanks for reporting this. The current behavior of joining all system messages into a single block is definitely a problem when part of the system prompt is dynamic (e.g., advisor-injected RAG context) — as you mentioned above, you end up paying 1.25x write cost on every request with zero cache benefit.

We went with a `multiBlockSystemCaching` flag on `AnthropicCacheOptions` that, when enabled, emits each `SystemMessage` as its own content block and places `cache_control` on the second-to-last one. This way the static prefix stays cached and the last block (dynamic content) can change freely without invalidating it. When there's only one system message, it behaves the same as before.

The flag defaults to `false`, so nothing changes for existing users. All the changes are contained within the anthropic module, this way we don't break any Spring AI core level APIs to support this anthropic only feature.

 Here is the PR: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/pull/5495

We would greatly appreciate if you can take a look and give any feedback. 

Thanks!

comments.author: CalamityAdam
comments.body:
This is a fantastic turnaround — thank you @sobychacko!

The `multiBlockSystemCaching` API in #5495 is exactly what we needed. The design is clean: keeping it as a boolean on `AnthropicCacheOptions` (rather than touching the core `Message` API) is the right call for containment, and defaulting to `false` means zero risk for existing users.

The second-to-last block placement for `cache_control` maps perfectly to our use case. We have ~2,280 static tokens of behavioral instructions (safety guardrails, brand tone, mode instructions, formatting) in the first `SystemMessage`, and Spring AI advisors inject dynamic context (RAG-matched product recommendations, intent/slot state) that changes every request. With this flag, the static prefix would stay cached at 0.1x read cost while the dynamic tail changes freely — exactly the Anthropic API capability we couldn't reach through the framework.

Our current workaround (moving dynamic advisor content from system to user messages) ships now and works well, but once this lands we'd be able to restore the semantic distinction without sacrificing cacheability. Really appreciate the backport label to 1.1.x as well — that's the version we're on.

One minor observation: the current implementation assumes the last `SystemMessage` is the dynamic one. In our case that holds true (static instructions are registered first, advisors append dynamic content after). Worth noting in the docs that message ordering matters — the second-to-last block gets `cache_control`, so users need to ensure their static content comes first.

comments.author: sobychacko
comments.body: @CalamityAdam Good point on the ordering — the implementation does assume the last `SystemMessage` is the dynamic one, which holds when static instructions are registered first and advisors append after. I've added an explicit note about this to the docs in the PR. Thanks for the feedback!

comments.body: @CalamityAdam As discussed on the PR, this is now addressed in both `main` (SDK) and `1.1.x`. Please let us know if you see any issues. Thanks!

comments.author: hbsjz-swl
comments.body:
You misunderstood the extra_body parameter of the Python OpenAI SDK.                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
extra_body is an SDK layer parameter in the Python OpenAI SDK. Its purpose is to expand and merge the content into the top layer of the request body, rather than sending it as a nested "extra_body" field.                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
  Python ：                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
 ```
 client.chat.completions.create(                                                                                                                                                                                                       
      model="qwen-plus",
      messages=[...],
      extra_body={"enable_search": True}
  )
```

The actual HTTP request body sent is：
```
  {
    "model": "qwen-plus",
    "messages": [...],
    "enable_search": true
  }
```

  Instead of：
  ```
{
    "model": "qwen-plus",
    "messages": [...],
    "extra_body": {"enable_search": true}
  }
```

  This is consistent with the behavior of Spring AI's @JsonAnyGetter—both expand the Map content to the top level.

title: The currentSize accumulation in TokenCountBatchingStrategy is inaccurate

comments.author: weiguangli-io
comments.body:
Submitted a fix in #5528.

Root cause: when `currentSize > maxInputTokenCount` triggers a new batch, `currentSize` resets to `0` but the triggering document still gets added to the new batch — so its token count is silently dropped from the running total.

Fix: reset `currentSize = entry.getValue()` instead of `0`.

title: Zhipu Model returns "network_error"/"sensitive" finish_reason which is not supported by ChatCompletionFinishReason in Spring AI 1.1.2
body:
### Description
I encountered an issue when using the Zhipu (GLM) model with Spring AI 1.1.2. 

The Zhipu API returns a response containing finish_reason values like "network_error" (or "sensitive") which are not defined in the `ChatCompletionFinishReason` enum of Spring AI 1.1.2. 

#### Example Response from Zhipu API:
{
  "id":"202603031103252ba2e084c0074fc3",
  "created":1772507037,
  "model":"GLM-5",
  "choices":[
    {
      "index":0,
      "finish_reason":"network_error",
      "delta":{"role":"assistant","content":""}
    }
  ]
}

#### Error Scenario:
When Spring AI attempts to map the "network_error" (or "sensitive") value from the Zhipu API response to the `ChatCompletionFinishReason` enum, it throws an exception (e.g., `IllegalArgumentException` or `EnumConstantNotPresentException`) because these values are not part of the enum's valid options.

### Expected Behavior
Spring AI should handle unsupported finish_reason values from Zhipu model gracefully (e.g., map to a "UNKNOWN" or "OTHER" enum value) instead of throwing an error.

### Actual Behavior
An exception is thrown due to unrecognized finish_reason values ("network_error"/"sensitive") that are not in `ChatCompletionFinishReason`.

### Environment
- Spring AI Version: 1.1.2
- Zhipu Model: GLM-5
- JDK Version: 21

comments.author: demo-zexuan
Hj7e2
comments.body:
> ## The Problem
> ZhipuAI (GLM) API returns `finish_reason` values like `"network_error"` and `"sensitive"` that don't exist in Spring AI's `ChatCompletionFinishReason` enum. This causes deserialization errors when Spring AI tries to parse these responses.
> 
> **Example response from Zhipu API:**
> 
> {
>   "id":"202603031103252ba2e084c0074fc3",
>   "created":1772507037,
>   "model":"GLM-5",
>   "choices":[
>     {
>       "index":0,
>       "finish_reason":"network_error",
>       "delta":{"role":"assistant","content":""}
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ## What I Found
> **Official documentation is pretty sparse here.** I searched through BigModel's docs (https://docs.bigmodel.cn) but couldn't find a complete list of all possible `finish_reason` values.
> 
> The standard values you'd expect based on OpenAI compatibility:
> 
> Value	Description
> `stop`	Model naturally completed or hit a stop sequence
> `length`	Hit max_tokens limit, output was truncated
> `tool_calls`	Model decided to call a tool
> `content_filter`	Content was blocked by safety filters
> `null`	Still generating (in streaming responses)
> But `"network_error"` and `"sensitive"`? Nowhere to be found in the docs. These could be:
> 
> 1. Newly added values not yet documented
> 2. Undocumented internal error codes
> 3. Edge cases that slipped through
> 
> ## Root Cause
> In `ZhiPuAiApi.java:408-436`, the `ChatCompletionFinishReason` enum only defines:
> 
> * `STOP` (`@JsonProperty("stop")`)
> * `LENGTH` (`@JsonProperty("length")`)
> * `CONTENT_FILTER` (`@JsonProperty("content_filter")`)
> * `TOOL_CALLS` (`@JsonProperty("tool_calls")`)
> * `TOOL_CALL` (`@JsonProperty("tool_call")`)
> 
> Missing: `UNKNOWN` to handle unknown values gracefully.
> 
> ## The Fix
> OpenAI already solved this elegantly by adding an `UNKNOWN` enum value:
> 
> // OpenAiApi.java:785-786
> @JsonProperty("")
> UNKNOWN,
> We should apply the same fix to `ZhiPuAiApi.ChatCompletionFinishReason`:
> 
> public enum ChatCompletionFinishReason {
>     /**
>      * Handles empty, NULL and unknown values
>      */
>     @JsonProperty("")
>     UNKNOWN,
>     // ... existing values
> }
> ## Impact
> * **Severity**: Medium
> * **Affected Users**: Anyone using ZhipuAI (GLM) models in Spring AI
> * **Trigger Condition**: When Zhipu API returns `network_error` or `sensitive` as `finish_reason`
> 
> This causes the entire request to fail instead of gracefully handling the edge case - not ideal for production systems.
> 
> ## Affected Components
> 1. **ZhiPuAiApi.java** - `ChatCompletionFinishReason` enum (lines 408-436)
> 2. **Streaming response handling** - `ChatCompletionChunk.ChunkChoice` (line 1122)
> 3. **Non-streaming response handling** - `ChatCompletion.Choice` (line 988)
> 
> ## Other Models with Same Issue
> The following models may have similar issues since they also lack the `UNKNOWN` value:
> 
> * DeepSeek
> * MiniMax
> * Mistral AI

I can find it on the webpage https://docs.bigmodel.cn/api-reference/%E6%A8%A1%E5%9E%8B-api/%E5%AF%B9%E8%AF%9D%E8%A1%A5%E5%85%A8
choices.finish_reason
string
推理终止原因。'stop’表示自然结束或触发stop词，'tool_calls’表示模型命中函数，'length’表示达到token长度限制，'sensitive’表示内容被安全审核接口拦截（用户应判断并决定是否撤回公开内容），'network_error’表示模型推理异常。

title: OpenAiModel internalCall does not have reasoningContent
body:
When using OpenAiChatModel in Spring AI, the internalCall method does not include reasoningContent in the returned ChatResponse metadata.

Even when the underlying OpenAI response contains reasoning-related content (e.g., from reasoning-capable models), the ChatResponse.getMetadata() does not expose it. As a result, users cannot access reasoning output via the Spring AI abstraction layer.

This appears to be a mapping omission in OpenAiChatModel.internalCall.

Environment
Spring AI version: 1.1.2

title: Add `@Nullable` to `value` parameter in `ChatClientResponse.Builder.context(String key, Object value)` for consistency
body:
**Summary**

`ChatClientResponse.Builder` has a method `context(String key, Object value)` where the `value` parameter is not annotated with `@Nullable`. The same overload in `ChatClientRequest.Builder` uses `context(String key, @Nullable Object value)`, and the context map type is `Map<String, @Nullable Object>` in both cases, so null values are allowed. Adding `@Nullable` to the response builder would align the two APIs and better reflect the actual contract.

**Current behavior**

- `ChatClientRequest.Builder.context(String key, @Nullable Object value)` — value is `@Nullable`
- `ChatClientResponse.Builder.context(String key, Object value)` — value has no nullability annotation

**Proposed change**

In `spring-ai-client-chat` → `ChatClientResponse.java`, change:

```java
public Builder context(String key, Object value) {
```

to:

```java
public Builder context(String key, @Nullable Object value) {
```

**Rationale**

- Consistency with `ChatClientRequest.Builder.context(String, @Nullable Object)`.
- The stored context is `Map<String, @Nullable Object>`, so the parameter semantics should allow null.
- Improves static analysis / IDE null-safety and documents the API contract.

**Scope**

- Single line change (add `@Nullable` to the parameter). No behavior change; `Assert.notNull` is only applied to `key`.

title: Regression with Deepseek and null content
body:
## Description

A null-safety regression was introduced in `DeepSeekStreamFunctionCallingHelper.merge()` between Spring AI 1.x and 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT, causing streaming to fail with `Content must not be null` whenever DeepSeek responds with a tool call (where `content` is `null` in the streaming delta).

## Root Cause

**Spring AI 1.x** (null-safe):
```java
String content = (current.content() != null
    ? (previous.content() != null ? previous.content() + current.content() : current.content())
    : (previous.content() != null ? previous.content() : ""));
```

**Spring AI 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT** (`DeepSeekStreamFunctionCallingHelper.java` line 82, regressed):
```java
String content = previous != null ? previous.content() + current.content() : current.content();
```

When DeepSeek returns a streaming chunk for a tool call, `current.content()` is `null`. With the 2.0 code:
- If `previous == null` (first chunk): `content = null`
- If `previous != null`: `previous.content() + null` concatenates to `"...null"`

The `null` content then propagates and hits `Assert.notNull(content, "Content must not be null")` downstream, terminating the stream with an exception.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a DeepSeek streaming client with Spring AI 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT
2. Register a tool/function on the chat client
3. Send a user message that triggers DeepSeek to call the tool
4. Observe: `Content must not be null` exception, stream never completes

## Expected Behavior

The null-safe fallback from 1.x should be restored: when `current.content()` is `null`, fall back to `previous.content()`, and ultimately to `""`.

## Suggested Fix

Restore the null-safe expression from 1.x in `DeepSeekStreamFunctionCallingHelper.merge(ChatCompletionMessage, ChatCompletionMessage)`:

```java
String content = (current.content() != null
    ? (previous != null && previous.content() != null ? previous.content() + current.content() : current.content())
    : (previous != null && previous.content() != null ? previous.content() : ""));
```

## Environment

- Spring AI: `2.0.0-SNAPSHOT` (build `20260306.171833-166`)
- DeepSeek model: `deepseek-chat`
- Spring Boot: `4.0.3`
- Spring Framework: `7.x`

title: Add LostInTheMiddleReorderDocumentPostProcessor
body:
**Expected Behavior**
A built-in  DocumentPostProcessor implementation that reorders retrieved documents to mitigate the "Lost in the Middle" problem, placing the most relevant documents at the extremities of the context window.

``` java
DocumentPostProcessor reorder = new LostInTheMiddleReorderDocumentPostProcessor();

var advisor = RetrievalAugmentationAdvisor.builder()
    .documentRetriever(VectorStoreDocumentRetriever.builder()
        .vectorStore(vectorStore)
        .topK(10)
        .build())
    .documentPostProcessors(reorder)
    .build();
```
Given documents sorted by descending relevance [D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, D6], the processor should return [D1, D3, D5, D6, D4, D2] — most and least relevant documents placed at the boundaries of the context.

**Current Behavior**
The DocumentPostProcessor interface exists in spring-ai-rag but has no built-in implementations. The official documentation explicitly mentions the "lost-in-the-middle" problem as a target use case for DocumentPostProcessor:

> "A component for post-processing retrieved documents based on a query, addressing challenges such as lost-in-the-middle, context length restrictions from the model, and the need to reduce noise and redundancy."

However, users must currently implement this entirely from scratch with no reference implementation to follow.

**Context**
When using MultiQueryExpander with a large topK, we often get many documents. Simply sorting them by relevance score (like ConcatenationDocumentJoiner does) places moderately relevant documents consecutively in the middle, which the LLM might underutilize.

Since this is just a pure-Java reordering of the list, it requires no LLM calls or additional dependencies. It would be a small, self-contained implementation following the existing RAG module conventions (Builder pattern, Asserts, etc.).

I'd love to work on this and submit a PR as my first contribution to Spring AI. Would a PR for this be welcome? Let me know what you think!

title: `ChatClient` creation best practices
body:
I am reading https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/2.0/api/chatclient.html#_creating_a_chatclient and have some opinions;

## The first section "Using an autoconfigured ChatClient.Builder"
This is spot on imo 👍 

## Then off to "Multiple ChatClients with a Single Model Type"
In this case I think one would still be able to use the auto-configured `ChatClient.Builder` and just clone and modify it, e.g.;
```java
        ChatClient chatClient = chatClientBuilder.build();

        ChatClient customChatClient = chatClientBuilder.clone()
                .defaultSystem("You are a helpful assistant.")
                .build();
```

(Btw, the current docs uses the `defaultSystemPrompt(String)` method on the builder, but it doesn't exist).

## Next up the "ChatClients for Different Model Types" section
Here I agree that we really need to bypass the auto-configured `ChatClient.Builder`. However, when we do so it has a couple of side effects;
1. Observability is completely disabled for the mode
2. `ChatClientCustomizer` beans are ignored

I think it would be a good idea if the docs clearly pointed out those side effects (especially the observability thing would be a no-no in enterprise deployments imo), and maybe also show how to avoid the side effects by creating the custom/ad-hoc builder similar to how [`ChatClientAutoConfiguration`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/auto-configurations/models/chat/client/spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-chat-client/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/model/chat/client/autoconfigure/ChatClientAutoConfiguration.java#L88-L99) does it?

My point is that, imo, just doing `ChatClient.builder(myChatModel)` should be avoided as much as possible in order to ensure we have proper observability (and customizers applied), but it is not clear from the current docs.
