title: Feature request: stateful agent graph orchestration
body:
## Problem

Spring AI provides low-level primitives (`ChatClient`, `ToolCallback`, `Advisor`, `ChatMemory`) but no higher-level layer to build multi-step agents. Today, developers must hand-write the execution loop, manage state, persist it, and implement human-in-the-loop patterns on their own. This leads to duplicated and fragile code across projects.

## Proposal

Add a new module `spring-ai-graph` with six primitives to compose agents declaratively:

**1. State** — typed immutable container passed between steps

```java
public record AgentState(
    List<Message> messages,
    Map<String, Object> scratchpad,
    @Nullable String nextStep
) {}
```

**2. Node** — a function `State -> State`

```java
@AgentNode("plan")
public AgentState plan(AgentState state) {
    return state.withNextStep("execute");
}
```

**3. Edge** — linear and conditional transitions, cycles allowed

```java
AgentGraph graph = AgentGraph.builder()
    .addNode("plan", planner)
    .addNode("execute", executor)
    .addNode("respond", responder)
    .addEdge("plan", "execute")
    .addConditionalEdge("execute",
        state -> state.isDone() ? "respond" : "plan")
    .build();
```

**4. Checkpointer** — pluggable persistence

```java
.checkpointer(new JdbcCheckpointer(dataSource))
```

Reference implementations: `InMemoryCheckpointer`, `JdbcCheckpointer`, `RedisCheckpointer`.

**5. Interrupt / Resume** — native human-in-the-loop

```java
@AgentNode("approve")
@Interrupt
public AgentState approve(AgentState state) {
    return state;
}

graph.invoke(state, threadId);
graph.resume(threadId, Map.of("approved", true));
```

**6. Trace** — built-in tracing using OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions

```java
.enableTrace(TraceConfig.builder()
    .captureInput(true)
    .captureOutput(true)
    .captureLlmCalls(true)
    .captureToolCalls(true)
    .exporter(new OtelExporter())
    .build())
```

## Why this belongs in the framework

Without these primitives, every team rewrites:

- the agent loop (`while` + state bean)
- checkpointing (manual serialization)
- HITL (ad-hoc endpoints)
- tracing (inconsistent span names)

Observability in particular must be transparent: the developer writes `@AgentNode`, the framework wraps each execution in a span automatically. If left to the developer, there is no common convention.

## Scope

In scope:
- `spring-ai-graph` module with the six primitives
- Two reference checkpointers: `InMemory`, `Jdbc`
- OpenTelemetry integration
- ReAct and plan-execute examples

Out of scope (future issues):
- Multi-agent collaboration
- Graph visualization UI
- Semantic / long-term memory

## Alternatives

- **Keep Advisors only** — linear, no cycles, not suitable for agent loops.
- **Reuse Spring State Machine** — no native understanding of messages, tokens, tool calls.
- **Delegate to LangGraph4j** — community project, not integrated with `ChatClient` or Spring auto-configuration.

## Prior art

- LangGraph (Python, JS)
- LlamaIndex Workflows
- Semantic Kernel Process Framework

All three use the same six primitives.

## Open questions

- Should `AgentGraph` consume `ChatClient` directly, or orchestrate multiple `ChatClient` instances at a higher level?
- Conditional edges: functional `Predicate<State>` or named routing functions?
- Should `@Interrupt` be a method annotation or a dedicated `InterruptNode` type?
- How should checkpointing interact with `ChatMemoryRepository` to avoid duplication?

Feedback on API shape and module boundaries welcome before any implementation.

**Update: Contributor Reputation Action now available**

While building governance tooling for the [Agent Governance Toolkit](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit), we uncovered a pattern of coordinated inauthentic contributions targeting AI agent frameworks. Accounts use a credibility-laundering pipeline: getting small PRs merged in one repo, then citing those merges as credentials in spray issues across dozens of other repos.

We built and shipped open-source tooling to detect these patterns, now available as a **reusable GitHub Action** any repo can adopt:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/contributor-check.yml
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened]
  issues:
    types: [opened]

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit/.github/actions/contributor-check@main
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          target-repo: microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit
```

**What it does:**
- Checks contributor account shape (age, repo count, follower ratio)
- Detects credential-spray patterns (merged PRs cited across other repos)
- Labels and comments on MEDIUM/HIGH risk contributions for maintainer review
- Zero external dependencies (Python stdlib only)

The tools are MIT-licensed at [`microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit/scripts/`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit/tree/main/scripts) and shipped in AGT v3.3.0.

Sharing as a heads-up since AI agent repos are prime targets for this kind of campaign. Happy to help with integration if useful.

comments.author: paulbakker
comments.body:
At Netflix we use dependency locking through Nebula (Gradle), which aligns requested dependency versions and locks to a single version. Without intervention it picks the highest requested version.

If Spring AI has a transitive dependency on Boot 4.1, and application that directly requests Boot 4.0, will actually get Boot 4.1 because Spring AI requests it.

```
ExampleApp (Resolves Spring Boot 4.1, because Spring AI requests it)
|- Spring AI 2.x
|---- Spring Boot 4.1
|- Spring Boot 4.0
```

I actually thought the same would happen on projects not using Nebula, but that doesn't seem to be the case after testing this with a new Spring Initialzr project.

We typically (e.g. DGS framework) put the _lowest_ supported version as our build dependencies, and explicitly add a test module for any newer versions we would also want to support. We do this because our OSS users also see classpath leakage, but it is dependent on what build/locking tooling you're using.

Btw, it works fine with 4.0 after explicitly forcing it to the correct version.

title: DefaultChatOptionsBuilder.combineWith does not defensively copy stopSequences
body:
**Bug description**

`DefaultChatOptionsBuilder.combineWith(ChatOptions.Builder<?>)` assigns the
source builder's `stopSequences` reference directly instead of making a
defensive copy, leaving two builders sharing the same underlying
`List<String>` after a combine:

https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/main/spring-ai-model/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/chat/prompt/DefaultChatOptionsBuilder.java#L133-L135

```java
if (that.stopSequences != null) {
    this.stopSequences = that.stopSequences;   // shared reference
}
```

Every other mutation path in the same class performs a defensive copy, and
the defensive-copy policy is already asserted by an existing unit test:

- `stopSequences(List<String>)` setter — `new ArrayList<>(stop)` (L92)
- `clone()` — `new ArrayList<>(this.stopSequences)` (L52)
- `ChatOptionsBuilderTests.shouldPreserveCopyIntegrity` — asserts that external mutations to a caller-supplied list must not leak into the built `ChatOptions`

`combineWith` is the only mutation path on the builder that does not honor this policy, leaving a latent shared-state bug. A related class of "mutable collection shared across instances" was previously addressed in #4117.

**Environment**

- Spring AI: `2.0.0-SNAPSHOT` (current `main`, commit `d199dbcb7`)
- Module: `spring-ai-model`
- Java: OpenJDK 21.0.10 (aarch64)
- OS: macOS 14 (darwin 23.6.0)
- Vector store: N/A — pure builder logic, environment-independent.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Create a `ChatOptions.Builder` `source` and set a non-null `stopSequences` list on it.
2. Create a second `ChatOptions.Builder` `target` and call `target.combineWith(source)`.
3. Inspect the internal `stopSequences` field on both builders — they point to the same `List` instance. Any in-place mutation on that list (e.g. via `DefaultChatOptions.setStopSequences(mutableList)` on an options object built from either builder, followed by `mutableList.add(...)`) becomes observable from both builders.

**Expected behavior**

After `combineWith`, `source` and `target` should hold **independent** `stopSequences` lists, consistent with the setter, `clone()`, and the policy asserted by `shouldPreserveCopyIntegrity`. Mutating the list held by one builder must not be observable from the other.

**Minimal Complete Reproducible example**

Test added in the same package so it can inspect the `protected` `stopSequences` field directly — the public `getStopSequences()` returns a `Collections.unmodifiableList` wrapper and hides reference identity:

```java
@Test
void combineWithShouldDefensivelyCopyStopSequences() {
    ChatOptions.Builder source = ChatOptions.builder().stopSequences(List.of("STOP"));
    ChatOptions.Builder target = ChatOptions.builder();
    target.combineWith(source);

    DefaultChatOptionsBuilder<?> sourceImpl = (DefaultChatOptionsBuilder<?>) source;
    DefaultChatOptionsBuilder<?> targetImpl = (DefaultChatOptionsBuilder<?>) target;

    assertThat(targetImpl.stopSequences).containsExactly("STOP");
    assertThat(targetImpl.stopSequences).isNotSameAs(sourceImpl.stopSequences);
}
```

Verified locally against current `main` (commit `d199dbcb7`):

- **Fails without the fix** — the `isNotSameAs` assertion throws `AssertionError`.
- **Passes** when L133–135 becomes `this.stopSequences = new ArrayList<>(that.stopSequences);`.
- No regression in the other 15 tests in `ChatOptionsBuilderTests`.

Happy to open a PR with the one-line fix and this test once triaged.

title: Tool inputSchema with recursive parameter types emits unresolvable `$ref` (nested `$defs`, root-relative `$ref`)

comments.author: jeanchristophecascade
comments.body:
Confirming this bug also affects the **MCP-specific** schema path. Spring AI's `mcp/mcp-annotations/.../McpJsonSchemaGenerator.java` has separate code with the same `SUBTYPE_SCHEMA_GENERATOR` wiring as `spring-ai-model`'s `JsonSchemaGenerator`, and reproduces the issue identically against any MCP tool whose input takes a nested data class.

**Reproduced on Spring AI 2.0.0-M5** with `spring-ai-starter-mcp-server-webmvc` + Kotlin / JDK 25:

- `commitChanges(ops: List<ChangeOp>)` where `ChangeOp.CreateOp` carries `properties: Map<String, Any?>` → `$defs/Map_String.Object_` nested in `ops`, root-relative `$ref`.
- `findParties(role: RoleFilter, ...)` and `findRoles(filter: RoleFilter, ...)` where `RoleFilter` has `for: PartyFilter?` and `of: PartyFilter?` → `$defs/PartyFilter` nested in `role`/`filter`, root-relative `$ref` to both `for` and `of`.

`tools/list` looks plausible in all cases; `tools/call` fails NetworkNT validation (the resolver Spring's MCP SDK uses) with *"Reference /$defs/PartyFilter cannot be resolved"* exactly when the agent passes a value at the `$ref` location.

**Suggesting any fix lands in both files in the same PR:**
- `models/spring-ai-model/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/util/json/schema/JsonSchemaGenerator.java` (the file this issue is reported against)
- `mcp/mcp-annotations/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/mcp/annotation/method/tool/utils/McpJsonSchemaGenerator.java`

Both build per-parameter sub-schemas the same way:

```java
ObjectNode parameterNode = SUBTYPE_SCHEMA_GENERATOR.generateSchema(parameterType);
// ...
properties.set(parameterName, parameterNode);
```

The hoist-`$defs`-to-root snippet in this issue's "Suggested fix" applies cleanly to both.

For anyone hitting this on M5 today: a `BeanPostProcessor` watching the `toolSpecs` bean and rewriting each `Tool.inputSchema` via a recursive `$defs`-hoist works as a drop-in user-side workaround.

comments.author: jewoodev
comments.body:
While working on #6035, I noticed a related but distinct variant: a directly self-recursive parameter type can produce `$ref: "#"`, which has a different failure mode from the transitive `$defs` case reported here.

#6035 focuses on the reported transitive-recursion case, where a parameter sub-schema contains its own `$defs` but keeps root-relative `#/$defs/...` references after being inlined into the method-input schema. Fixing that case can be done by hoisting `$defs` to the outer root.

The direct `$ref: "#"` variant likely needs a different rewrite strategy, so I’m keeping it out of #6035 to avoid mixing two fixes in one PR.

comments.author: jewoodev
comments.body:
Hi @ningmd, I traced the 400 to where a streaming turn loses `reasoning_content` — the streaming sibling of the non-streaming reasoning round-trip in #6026.

In the OpenAI-compatible path (`OpenAiChatModel`), the round-trip breaks during chunk merge, before aggregation:

- `ChunkMerger.chunkToChatCompletion` rebuilds the message from `content`/`refusal`/`toolCalls` only, and `mergeDeltas` merges tool calls only, so the `reasoning_content` carried on each `delta` is never copied onto the merged message — the chunk-level `putAllAdditionalProperties` lands on the `ChatCompletion`, not the message that `getReasoningContent` reads.
- `getReasoningContent` then finds no `reasoning_content` in `message._additionalProperties()` and returns empty, so the assistant message's `reasoningContent` metadata stays empty and the replay in `createRequest` has nothing to re-attach on the next turn — hence the 400.

This is independent of tool calling; the tool case is just where DeepSeek requires `reasoning_content` to be present. On current `main` the non-streaming (`call`) path does capture it (via `getReasoningContent`) and replay it in `createRequest` (wired in `b1df49934`) — only streaming drops it before capture.

I saw @i-zoufeng offered to fix this — happy to support that, or to take a focused PR carrying `reasoning_content` through to the aggregated `AssistantMessage` so the existing replay can re-attach it, with a test asserting it survives aggregation. One thing that would pinpoint the fix: are you on the `spring-ai-starter-model-openai` starter or the native `-deepseek` one? They take different streaming routes — `spring-ai-starter-model-openai` hits the `ChunkMerger` gap above, while the native `-deepseek` path does capture `reasoning_content` on `DeepSeekAssistantMessage`, but the shared `MessageAggregator` rebuilds the message into a plain `AssistantMessage` and drops that typed field, so the next-turn replay has nothing to re-attach. That tells us where the fix belongs. Happy to go a different direction if you'd prefer.

title: Add a document reranking post-processor for Modular RAG flows
body:
## Overview

Spring AI's Modular RAG architecture already exposes a `DocumentPostProcessor` extension point for post-retrieval document processing.

One common RAG pattern is to retrieve a broader candidate set from a vector store, rerank those candidates with a more precise relevance signal, and then pass only the highest-ranked documents to generation.

Currently, users need to implement this pattern manually for each application. A reusable reranking post-processor would make this flow easier to configure and align it with the existing RAG module abstractions.

## Proposal

Add a reusable document reranking post-processor for Modular RAG flows.

The reranking component would not prescribe a ranking strategy. Instead, users can provide their own `DocumentReranker` implementation.

For example, users could

- Call an external reranking provider such as Cohere, Jina, Voyage, or another cross-encoder service
- Sort by a custom score derived from document metadata, freshness, authority, or business priority
- Apply simple rule-based ranking for application-specific constraints
- Combine vector similarity scores, keyword matches, metadata scores, and external model scores
- Reduce the final context size by keeping only the top N reranked documents

## Scope

- Add `DocumentReranker` as a small functional contract under the RAG post-retrieval document package
- Add `RerankingDocumentPostProcessor` as a `DocumentPostProcessor` implementation
- Add optional `topN` support to keep only the first N reranked documents
- Add unit tests covering reranking behavior, `topN`, validation, and empty input handling
- Update the RAG documentation with a basic `RetrievalAugmentationAdvisor` configuration example

## Example Usage

```java
@Bean
Advisor retrievalAugmentationAdvisor(VectorStore vectorStore, DocumentReranker documentReranker) {
    return RetrievalAugmentationAdvisor.builder()
        .documentRetriever(VectorStoreDocumentRetriever.builder()
            .vectorStore(vectorStore)
            .topK(20)
            .build())
        .documentPostProcessors(RerankingDocumentPostProcessor.builder()
            .documentReranker(documentReranker)
            .topN(5)
            .build())
        .build();
}
```

## Expected Outcome

Users can retrieve a broad candidate set, rerank it using their preferred strategy or provider, and keep the top N documents before query augmentation.

This improves context precision while preserving the recall benefits of retrieving more candidates from the vector store.

**`ConcurrentHashMap` doesn't support storing `null` value.** So,

- If you want to call the `.keyValue("system_fingerprint", null)`, this key-value pair will be ignored, then `metadata.containsKey("system_fingerprint")` will return `false`.
- If you want `metadata.containsKey("system_fingerprint")` to return `true`, you must use an `Object` as placeholders to represent the `null` value in `ConcurrentHashMap`, or even replace the `ConcurrentHashMap`.

| Plan | `.containsKey()` return | `.get()` return | Complexity | Comprehensive and short summary |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| **A. Skip JSON null fields** | `false`❌ | `null`✅ | Low✅ | Minimal, low-risk fix. Preserves non-null extra fields like `provider`, but does not distinguish missing fields from JSON `null`. |
| **B. Internal sentinel for JSON null** | `true`✅ | `null`✅ | Medium✅ | Fully preserves JSON `null` semantics while keeping `ConcurrentHashMap`, but requires shared metadata changes. |
| **C. Replace `ConcurrentHashMap`** | `true`✅ | `null`✅ | High❌ | Simple null-preserving behavior, but changes the shared metadata map implementation and concurrency characteristics. |

Observations produced by the Spring AI OpenAI module are using "openai_sdk" as value for the provider name instead of "openai". All observations produced by the Spring AI OpenAI module should use "openai" as the provider name.

title: Add static factory shortcuts for low-ceremony agent creation
body:
## Motivation

The current Builder API takes ~16 lines for the 2-agent coordinator example shown in the README's *In 60 seconds* section. This verbosity hurts the time-to-aha for newcomers and the README pitch itself.

Spring AI exposes both `ChatClient.create(chatModel)` and `ChatClient.builder(...)` so callers can pick the right ceremony for their use case. spring-agent-flow should follow the same pattern.

## Before / after

### Before (16 lines)

```java
ExecutorAgent researcher = ExecutorAgent.builder()
        .chatClient(chatClient)
        .systemPrompt("Find key facts.")
        .build();

ExecutorAgent writer = ExecutorAgent.builder()
        .chatClient(chatClient)
        .systemPrompt("Write a clear report.")
        .build();

CoordinatorAgent coordinator = CoordinatorAgent.builder()
        .executors(Map.of("research", researcher, "writing", writer))
        .routingStrategy(RoutingStrategy.llmDriven(chatClient))
        .build();

AgentResult result = coordinator.execute(
        AgentContext.of("Compare Claude 4 and GPT-5"));

System.out.println(result.text());
```

### After (7 lines, same semantics)

```java
var researcher = ExecutorAgent.of(chatClient, "Find key facts.");
var writer    = ExecutorAgent.of(chatClient, "Write a clear report.");

var coordinator = CoordinatorAgent.of(chatClient, Map.of(
    "research", researcher,
    "writing",  writer));

System.out.println(coordinator.execute("Compare Claude 4 and GPT-5").text());
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ExecutorAgent.of(ChatClient chatClient, String systemPrompt)` static factory
- [ ] `ExecutorAgent.of(ChatClient chatClient, String name, String systemPrompt)` overload (when a name is needed)
- [ ] `CoordinatorAgent.of(ChatClient chatClient, Map<String, Agent> executors)` static factory, defaulting to `RoutingStrategy.llmDriven(chatClient)`
- [ ] `Agent.execute(String userMessage)` default method delegating to `execute(AgentContext.of(userMessage))`
- [ ] Existing `Builder` APIs unchanged (additive only, no breaking change)
- [ ] Unit tests covering each new factory / overload
- [ ] Update `spring-agent-flow-samples` `MultiAgentCoordination` to use the new shortcuts
- [ ] Update the *In 60 seconds* code block in README accordingly

## Non-goals

- DSL / fluent-builder DSL such as `Squad.named(...).agent(...)` — too much surface area for marginal gain
- Annotation-based agent declaration (`@AgentSquad`) — heavy machinery, debugger-hostile
- Kotlin-flavored API — out of scope for this issue

The `.of(...)` Java idiom is the sweet spot and matches Spring AI's `ChatClient.create()` pattern.

## Why this is a good first issue

- Additive only — no risk of breaking existing users
- Clear before / after metric (line count of the README sample)
- Touches three small files (`ExecutorAgent`, `CoordinatorAgent`, `Agent`) plus one sample plus the README
- Tests are straightforward (each factory is a thin wrapper over the existing builder)

comments.body:
## Suspection

I initially suspect that the Spring AI didn't follow the DeepSeek API Guide. DeepSeek thinking mode [requires `reasoning_content` to be passed back when tool calls are involved, otherwise it returns 400](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode#tool-calls).

> Please note that, unlike turns in thinking mode that do not involve tool calls, for turns that do perform tool calls, the reasoning_content must be fully passed back to the API in all subsequent requests.
>

title: Tool input schema marks Kotlin nullable fields as required in `JsonSchemaGenerator`
body:
### Bug description

Every `val ... = null` property of a Kotlin data class used inside a `@McpTool` parameter (or as the input/output of structured-output conversion) is emitted with `required: true` in the generated JSON Schema, regardless of nullability or default value.

The two schema generators involved are:
- `org.springframework.ai.util.json.schema.JsonSchemaGenerator` (spring-ai-model)
- `org.springframework.ai.mcp.annotation.method.tool.utils.McpJsonSchemaGenerator` (spring-ai-mcp-annotations)

Both initialise their victools `SchemaGenerator` with `JacksonSchemaModule + Swagger2Module + SpringAiSchemaModule` only — `org.springframework.ai.model.KotlinModule` (shipped via PR #1766 to resolve #1667 for `ModelOptionsUtils`) does not appear to be registered in either of these newer paths.

This is consistent with the fragmentation flagged in #5915 and the sibling cases in #4487 / #5341.

### Environment

Spring AI 2.0.0-M5, Kotlin 2.3, JDK 25, `spring-ai-starter-mcp-server-webmvc`.

### Steps to reproduce

```kotlin
data class Filter(val name: String? = null, val ids: List<String>? = null)

@McpTool(description = "...")
fun search(@McpToolParam(required = false) filter: Filter? = null): String = ""
```

`tools/list` returns:

```json
{
  "inputSchema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "filter": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": { "ids": { }, "name": { } },
        "required": ["ids", "name"]
      }
    },
    "required": []
  }
}
```

The top-level `required: []` is correct (param-level honours `@McpToolParam(required = false)` and `@org.jspecify.Nullable`). The nested `required: ["ids", "name"]` is the issue.

### Expected behavior

`required: []` (or absent) for the nested object — both fields are Kotlin-nullable constructor parameters with default values. This matches what `KotlinModule#isRequired` already computes:

```java
boolean isNonNullable = !returnType.isMarkedNullable();
boolean isInConstructor = constructorParamsWithoutDefault.contains(name);
return isNonNullable && isInConstructor;
```

### One possible approach

Registering `KotlinModule` in each generator's static initialiser when Kotlin is on the classpath:

```java
SchemaGeneratorConfigBuilder builder = new SchemaGeneratorConfigBuilder(...)
    .with(jacksonModule)
    .with(openApiModule)
    .with(springAiSchemaModule);
if (KotlinDetector.isKotlinReflectPresent()) {
    builder.with(new KotlinModule());
}
```

`spring-ai-model` is already a transitive dependency of `spring-ai-mcp-annotations`, so no new dependency would be required.

### Workaround

Annotate every nullable Kotlin data-class field with `@field:JsonProperty(required = false)` (Jackson 2 — recognised by victools' `JacksonSchemaModule` via `JacksonOption.RESPECT_JSONPROPERTY_REQUIRED`). Verbose but functional in 2.0.0-M5.

### Related

- #1667 / PR #1766 — original Kotlin support, scoped to `ModelOptionsUtils`.
- #4533 — same root cause, parameter-level scope.
- #4487 — sibling: `@McpTool` output schema generation also creates its own config and skips modules.
- #5341 — sibling: `BeanOutputConverter` ignores `@Schema`.
- #5915 — umbrella: consolidate JSON schema generation across paths.

After that PR is merged, there will still be issues with MCP Tools, though, and that can be addressed my making a similar change to `McpJsonSchemaGenerator`.

title: DeepSeekChatAutoConfiguration Does Not Respect `spring.ai.deepseek.chat.enabled` Property
body:
## Description
According to Spring AI official documentation, the property `spring.ai.deepseek.chat.enabled` should control whether the DeepSeek chat model is enabled. However, setting this property to `false` has no effect on the auto-configuration behavior.

The auto-configuration class `DeepSeekChatAutoConfiguration` only checks the `spring.ai.model.chat` property and ignores the `spring.ai.deepseek.chat.enabled` property entirely.

## Environment Information
- **Spring AI Version**: 2.0.0-M5
- **Spring Boot Version**: 4.0.6
- **Java Version**: 17

## Reproduction Steps

### Step 1: Configure Spring AI Dependencies
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.ai</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-ai-deepseek</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

### Step 2: Set Application Configuration
In `application.yaml`:
```yaml
spring:
  ai:
    deepseek:
      chat:
        enabled: false  # Attempt to disable DeepSeek
        # api-key: sk-xxx  # No API key configured
```

### Step 3: Start Application
Run the Spring Boot application.

## Expected Behavior
When `spring.ai.deepseek.chat.enabled` is set to `false`, the `DeepSeekChatAutoConfiguration` should be disabled, and the application should start successfully without requiring a DeepSeek API key.

## Actual Behavior
The application fails to start with the following error:
```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: DeepSeek API key must be set

```

## Root Cause Analysis

### Current Implementation
The `DeepSeekChatAutoConfiguration` class has the following conditional annotation:

```java
@AutoConfiguration
@ConditionalOnClass({DeepSeekApi.class})
@EnableConfigurationProperties({DeepSeekConnectionProperties.class, DeepSeekChatProperties.class})
@ConditionalOnProperty(
    name = {"spring.ai.model.chat"},
    havingValue = "deepseek",
    matchIfMissing = true
)
public class DeepSeekChatAutoConfiguration {
    // ...
}
```

### Issues Identified

 **Missing Property Check**: The configuration only checks `spring.ai.model.chat` but does not check `spring.ai.deepseek.chat.enabled`.

### Code Location
- **Class**: `org.springframework.ai.model.deepseek.autoconfigure.DeepSeekChatAutoConfiguration`

## Temporary Workarounds

### Workaround 1: Set Model Selection to Empty String
```yaml
spring:
  ai:
    model:
      chat: ""  # Disable DeepSeek by not matching "deepseek"
```

### Workaround 2: Exclude Auto-Configuration
```java
@SpringBootApplication(exclude = DeepSeekChatAutoConfiguration.class)
public class AiChatApplication {
    // ...
}
```

## Impact 
This issue prevents users from properly disabling DeepSeek auto-configuration using the documented property, leading to confusion and potential application startup failures.

The official documentation mentions `spring.ai.deepseek.chat.enabled` as a valid configuration property, but the implementation does not support it.

comments.author: yaner-here
comments.body:
This is an expected behavior mentioned in the updatelog.

https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/blob/f040fc6e586b9ba64c00cec8f272cfd0d6f0a724/spring-ai-docs/src/main/antora/modules/ROOT/pages/upgrade-notes.adoc?plain=1#L1447-L1456

In Spring AI 2.0, enabling or disabling model provider auto-configuration was moved to unified, cross-provider selection properties, for example:

```
spring.ai.model.chat=<model-provider|none>
```

Previously, each provider had its own boolean switch:

```
spring.ai.deepseek.chat.enabled: false
spring.ai.openai.chat.enabled: false
spring.ai.ollama.chat.enabled: false
```

Now the configuration selects the provider by model type:

```
spring.ai.model.chat: deepseek
```

Or disables chat model auto-configuration entirely:

```
spring.ai.model.chat: none
```

I guess the primary motivation is to make multi-provider scenarios clearer. `enabled=false` can only express “disable this provider,” but it does not clearly answer “which chat model provider should be active?” The unified `spring.ai.model.chat` property can both select a specific provider, such as DeepSeek/OpenAI/Ollama, and disable that model type by setting it to none.

comments.body: Even I'm facing the same issue. Please provide the fix or merge the given fix asap.

comments.author: lin667z
comments.body: # OpenAiChatModel blocks streaming due to `collectList()` in `internalStream()`, defeating SSE purpose ## Bug Description When using `OpenAiChatModel.stream()`, the underlying `internalStream()` implementation collects all stream chunks into a list using `.collectList().flatMapMany(...)`. This blocking behavior occurs even when no tool calls (Function Calling) are involved. As a result, downstream consumers (such as Spring WebFlux and Server-Sent Events) cannot emit tokens incrementally. The client receives nothing until the entire LLM response is fully generated, which completely defeats the purpose of streaming. ## Expected Behavior When streaming *without* tool calls, each `ChatCompletionChunk` should be emitted to the downstream `Flux` immediately as soon as it arrives from the provider, enabling true token-by-token Server-Sent Events (SSE) delivery to clients. ## Actual Behavior All chunks are collected into a `List` via `collectList()` inside `OpenAiChatModel.java`, and then re-emitted via `Flux.fromIterable(list)`. The downstream consumer receives the entire payload all at once only after the generation is 100% complete. ### Impact & Practical Problems: 1. **No Incremental Output:** Browsers/clients experience a long hang (10–30+ seconds for long responses) and see zero SSE events until the end of the generation. 2. **Read Timeouts on OpenAI-Compatible Providers:** When using slower or high-latency OpenAI-compatible services (e.g., DeepSeek, Zhipu GLM, Moonshot, Qwen), OkHttp’s read timeout triggers during the `collectList()` waiting period. This results in an `InterruptedIOException: timeout` wrapped in `OpenAIIoException: Stream failed`. ## Environment - **Spring AI Version:** `2.0.0-M6` (also persists in `1.1.6`) - **Java Version:** 17 - **OpenAI Java SDK:** `4.34.0` - **HTTP Transport:** OkHttp (Default) - **Affected Providers/Models:** Any OpenAI-compatible service with slower generation or specific extension fields (e.g., `deepseek-reasoner`, `glm-4`, `qwen-turbo`, `moonshot-v1`). ## Minimal Reproducible Example ### 1. Controller Endpoint ### 2. Service Implementation ## Suggested Fix / Code Location The issue resides in `OpenAiChatModel.java` (around line 369 in the current version) inside the `internalStream()` method. **Suggested Approach:** The `collectList()` should be conditional. If the response chunks do not contain any tool/function calls, the `Flux` should pass through the chunks immediately without aggregating them into a list first.

title: OpenAI auto-config startup fails when only a sub-prefix credential is set
body:
## Background

While digging into #1818 (`spring.ai.openai.image.api-key` alone fails the context), 
I traced the failure to how OpenAI auto-configuration gates itsmodel beans, 
not to anything image-specific. The same shape of bug applies
to chat, embedding, audio.speech, audio.transcription, and moderation —
`image` is just the first one that surfaced because that's the path the
original reporter took.

I'm filing this as a separate issue (with a follow-up PR) because the fix
touches all six sub-configurations and introduces a small new `Condition`,
which feels closer to a refactor than a single-bean bug fix. The change
closes #1818 as a consequence. Happy to fold it back into #1818 if you'd
prefer that flow.

## Reproduction

```yaml
# application.yml — startup fails with only this set
spring:
  ai:
    openai:
      image:
        api-key: sk-xxx
```

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: At least one credential source must be specified:
    credential (apiKey), workloadIdentity, or adminApiKey
    at com.openai.core.ClientOptions$Builder.effectiveCredential(ClientOptions.kt:503)
    ... (wrapped by Spring as BeanCreationException during context startup)
```

Substitute `chat`, `embedding`, `audio.speech`, `audio.transcription`, or
`moderation` for `image` above and the failure is identical — only the
failing sub-configuration changes. Programmatic credentials, the
`OPENAI_API_KEY` env var, and Microsoft Foundry passwordless setups
exhibit the same shape: one valid credential source, five other
sub-configurations still try to register and fail fast.

## Current behavior

The six OpenAI auto-configurations gate registration only on
`spring.ai.openai.api-key` (the common prefix), even though Spring AI
already accepts several other valid credential sources at the SDK level:

- `spring.ai.openai.<chat|image|embedding|audio.speech|audio.transcription|moderation>.api-key`
- a programmatic `Credential` set on `OpenAiCommonProperties` or any of the sub-`*Properties`
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` env var (default OpenAI endpoint)
- Microsoft Foundry endpoints, where the api-key may legitimately be absent because passwordless auth is used. Detected by any of:
    - `spring.ai.openai.microsoft-foundry=true`
    - `base-url` ending in `openai.azure.com` or `cognitiveservices.azure.com`
    - `microsoft-deployment-name`, `deployment-name`, or `microsoft-foundry-service-version` set

In all of these cases, all six `@Configuration` classes still register;
`OpenAiSetup` then fails fast on the sub-configurations that have no
usable credential, and the failure takes the whole application context
down before the working sub-configuration ever boots.

## Why a custom Condition

The first thing I tried was widening the existing `@ConditionalOnProperty` — the same shape that's been attempted before:

```java
@ConditionalOnProperty(
    prefix = "spring.ai.openai",
    name = { "api-key", "image.api-key" },
    matchIfMissing = false
)
```

That doesn't work: Spring Boot's `name = {a, b}` semantics is AND, not OR
— it matches only when both keys are set, which is the opposite of what
we need. The condition needs OR-of-credential-sources logic, which I don't
see a way to express declaratively without a custom `SpringBootCondition`.

## Proposed change

A single `OpenAiConnectionCondition` utility with one inner condition per
sub-configuration (`Chat`, `Image`, `Embedding`, `AudioSpeech`,
`AudioTranscription`, `Moderation`). Each one independently checks the
credential sources listed above with short-circuit OR semantics. If none
match, the corresponding `@Bean` does not register, and the rest of the
context boots normally.

The conditions sit on the `@Bean` method, not the `@Configuration` class,
so:

- `@EnableConfigurationProperties(OpenAi*Properties)` still runs — the properties bean stays available for other code that injects it.
- The existing model-selector `@ConditionalOnProperty(spring.ai.model.<kind>)` keeps working unchanged.

A working branch with this change and 13 tests covering each credential
source per sub-configuration is ready (all green on the
`spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-openai` module). I'll open the PR right
after this issue if the direction looks reasonable.

## Scope / non-goals

- No public API changes, no new dependencies.
- No behavior change for users who already set `spring.ai.openai.api-key` — that branch matches first, exactly as today.
- Closes #1818 as a side effect.
- Build status: the `spring-ai-autoconfigure-model-openai` module builds and tests cleanly in isolation. Full-repo `mvn compile` on `main` is currently red due to two unrelated upstream regressions (`OpenAiImageProperties` NullAway / JSpecify, `OpenAiChatModel.streaming(boolean)`); I'll file those together as a separate issue so the PR's CI signal isn't confused with this change.

title: WebMvcStreamableServerTransportProvider: NPE + ERROR log on malformed initialize payload (should be 400)
body:
**Bug description**
`WebMvcStreamableServerTransportProvider` (Streamable HTTP transport for the embedded MCP server) throws a `NullPointerException` and logs it at **ERROR** with a stack trace when a client sends a malformed `initialize` payload (e.g. `params: {}` instead of the spec-required `protocolVersion` + `capabilities` + `clientInfo`). It should validate the deserialized request and return a JSON-RPC `-32602` (Invalid params) without an ERROR-level log emission.

This matches how the same component already handles the `Accept` header check — that one returns a structured `-32601` error with a clear message and no server-side ERROR. The initialize-payload path should follow the same pattern.

**Environment**
- `spring-ai` `2.0.0-M6`
- `io.modelcontextprotocol.sdk:mcp` `2.0.0-M2` (transitive)
- Spring Boot `4.0.6`, JDK 21

**Steps to reproduce**
```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}'
```
(Any embedded `spring-ai-starter-mcp-server-webmvc` setup; no special config needed.)

**Expected behavior**
## Actual behavior

Server log:

```
2026-05-10T09:50:23.583+02:00  INFO 160265 --- [nio-8080-exec-1] i.m.server.McpAsyncServer                : Client initialize request - Protocol: null, Capabilities: null, Info: null
2026-05-10T09:50:23.588+02:00 ERROR 160265 --- [nio-8080-exec-1] .WebMvcStreamableServerTransportProvider : Failed to initialize session: null
2026-05-10T09:50:23.590+02:00 ERROR 160265 --- [nio-8080-exec-1] .WebMvcStreamableServerTransportProvider : Failed to deserialize message: message must not be empty
```

Client receives a generic error response; server emits stack-trace-bearing ERRORs for what is fundamentally a 4xx-class client mistake.

## Expected behavior

- Server validates the deserialized `InitializeRequest` (non-null, has `protocolVersion`, has `capabilities`, has `clientInfo`).
- On failure: respond with JSON-RPC error `-32602 Invalid params` and a message naming the missing field (e.g. `"initialize.params.protocolVersion is required"`).
- Log at **DEBUG** (or omit) — bad client payloads should not surface as server ERRORs.

## Why it matters

Any external prober, monitoring system, or out-of-date client can spam the server log with stack-trace-bearing ERRORs. At scale this:
- Defeats ERROR-rate alerting (signal drowned by noise).
- Inflates log-storage cost.
- Surfaces internal type names (`McpSchema$InitializeRequest`) and stack frames in production logs.

The strictness itself is correct (matches the MCP spec) — only the surfacing is inappropriate.

**Minimal Complete Reproducible example**
https://github.com/networkinss/spring-ai-ERROR-log-malformed-payload.git

comments.author: yaner-here
comments.body:
The request sends `initialize.params` as `{}` and be serialized into an `InitializeRequest`, but all required fields are null (such as `protocolVersion`, `capabilities`, and `clientInfo`). The thrown exception has no message, e.getMessage() is null, so the transport logs:

```
Failed to initialize session: null
```

After catching the initialization exception, the transport tries to build an internal JSON-RPC error using `e.getMessage()`. But `e.getMessage()` is null. The MCP SDK `McpError.Builder` requires a non-empty message, so the second Exception throws:

```
Failed to deserialize message: message must not be empty
```

comments.author: networkinss
comments.body:
This no longer reproduces on Spring AI 2.0.1 (also verified on 2.0.0 GA), which builds against MCP Java SDK 2.0.0.

  Re-running the original repro against the embedded WebMvc streamable server:

`  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}'`

  now returns HTTP 200 with a normal initialize result, and the server log contains no ERROR and no stack trace, only:

  WARN  io.modelcontextprotocol.spec.McpSchema: InitializeRequest: missing required fields during deserialization: protocolVersion -> '', capabilities -> {}, clientInfo -> {name='', version=''}
  WARN  io.modelcontextprotocol.server.McpAsyncServer: Client requested unsupported protocol version: , so the server will suggest the 2025-11-25 version instead

  The change comes from the MCP Java SDK.

The original complaint (NPE + ERROR-level stack traces for a client-side mistake) is resolved. 
From my side this issue can be closed as fixed upstream.

title: Preserve `ChatResponseMetadata` during OpenAI streaming aggregation
body: When aggregating streaming chunks in OpenAiChatModel, built-in fields like `rateLimit` and `promptMetadata` are dropped when building ChatResponseMetadata.

title: `reasoning_content` / `thinking` is received from the model but silently dropped when replaying conversation history
body:
### Summary

All current `ChatModel` implementations that support reasoning/thinking models correctly
extract `reasoning_content` (or `thinking`) from the model response and store it in
`AssistantMessage` metadata or a subclass field. However, when that same
`AssistantMessage` is serialised back into a follow-up request (i.e. replayed as
conversation history), the field is silently set to `null`. This breaks multi-turn
conversations with any model that requires `reasoning_content` to be echoed back in the
conversation history (DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3, etc.).

---

### Affected models

| ChatModel | Receives reasoning | Sends reasoning back |
|---|---|---|
| `OpenAiChatModel` (2.0.0-M4, OpenAiApi-based) | ✅ stored in `AssistantMessage` metadata key `"reasoningContent"` | ❌ hardcoded `null` in `createRequest()` |
| `OpenAiChatModel` (SNAPSHOT, openai-java SDK) | ✅ stored in `AssistantMessage` metadata key `"reasoningContent"` | ❌ `ChatCompletionAssistantMessageParam.Builder` never sets the thinking field |
| `DeepSeekChatModel` | ✅ stored in `DeepSeekAssistantMessage.reasoningContent` | ❌ hardcoded `null` as the 7th constructor argument in `createRequest()` |
| `OllamaChatModel` | ✅ stored in `AssistantMessage` metadata key `"thinking"` | ❌ `OllamaApi.Message.Builder.thinking()` is never called in `createRequest()` |

---

### Root cause

#### `OpenAiChatModel` (2.0.0-M4)

`createRequest()` constructs `ChatCompletionMessage` for `ASSISTANT` messages with the
`reasoningContent` constructor parameter hardcoded to `null`, regardless of what was
stored in the incoming `AssistantMessage`:

```java
// OpenAiChatModel.java (2.0.0-M4), createRequest(), ASSISTANT branch
return List.of(new ChatCompletionMessage(
    assistantMessage.getText(),
    ChatCompletionMessage.Role.ASSISTANT,
    null, null, toolCalls, null, audioOutput,
    null,
    null   // ← reasoning_content always null, metadata value ignored
));
```

The metadata is populated correctly on the receive side (line 322):
```java
"reasoningContent", choice.message().reasoningContent() != null ? choice.message().reasoningContent() : ""
```

#### `DeepSeekChatModel`

Same pattern. `DeepSeekAssistantMessage.getReasoningContent()` is never read back in
`createRequest()`. The 7th constructor argument is hardcoded `null` (line 426):

```java
return List.of(new ChatCompletionMessage(text, ChatCompletionMessage.Role.ASSISTANT,
    null, null, toolCalls, isPrefixAssistantMessage,
    null   // ← reasoning_content always null
));
```

The fix would be:
```java
String reasoningContent = (message instanceof DeepSeekAssistantMessage dsm)
    ? dsm.getReasoningContent() : null;
return List.of(new ChatCompletionMessage(text, ChatCompletionMessage.Role.ASSISTANT,
    null, null, toolCalls, isPrefixAssistantMessage, reasoningContent));
```

#### `OllamaChatModel`

`OllamaApi.Message.Builder` already has a `.thinking()` method (added for Qwen3 etc.),
but `createRequest()` never calls it (line 466):

```java
return List.of(OllamaApi.Message.builder(Role.ASSISTANT)
    .content(assistantMessage.getText())
    .toolCalls(toolCalls)
    // .thinking(...) ← never called, metadata value ignored
    .build());
```

The fix would be:
```java
String thinking = (String) assistantMessage.getMetadata().get("thinking");
return List.of(OllamaApi.Message.builder(Role.ASSISTANT)
    .content(assistantMessage.getText())
    .toolCalls(toolCalls)
    .thinking(thinking)
    .build());
```

---

### Impact

Any application using a reasoning model in a multi-turn / agentic loop will silently send
incomplete history to the model. Some providers (e.g. DeepSeek) explicitly require
`reasoning_content` to be present alongside `tool_calls` in assistant turns; omitting it
causes API errors or degraded model behaviour.

---

### Expected behaviour

When an `AssistantMessage` that was produced by a reasoning model is replayed as
conversation history, the `reasoning_content` / `thinking` field should be included in
the serialised request, exactly as it was received.

---

### Suggested fix

For each affected `ChatModel`, in the `ASSISTANT` branch of `createRequest()`:

1. Check whether the incoming `AssistantMessage` carries reasoning content
   (via subclass field or metadata key, depending on the model).
2. Pass that value to the corresponding request message field instead of `null`.

No new public API is needed; it is purely a missing read-through in the serialisation
path.

comments.author: liushenling2001
comments.body:
I can reproduce the `reasoning_content` replay problem on Spring AI `2.0.0-M7` as well, using `spring-ai-openai` with an OpenAI-compatible DeepSeek endpoint.

Environment:

- Spring AI: `2.0.0-M7`
- `spring-ai-openai` pulls `com.openai:openai-java:4.36.0`
- Model tested: `deepseek-v4-flash`
- Thinking enabled with `thinking: { "type": "enabled" }`

What I verified directly against the DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible API:

1. Thinking without tools works and returns both `reasoning_content` and `content`.
2. Thinking with a tool call works when the next request replays the assistant message with both `tool_calls` and the original `reasoning_content`.
3. The same second request fails with HTTP 400 when `reasoning_content` is omitted from the replayed assistant message.

The failure is consistent with DeepSeek's documented requirement that `reasoning_content` must be passed back in thinking mode when continuing the conversation.

This matters for `spring-ai-openai`, not only `spring-ai-deepseek`: in `OpenAiChatModel.createRequest(...)`, the assistant-history branch serializes `content` and `tool_calls`, but vendor-specific assistant fields such as DeepSeek's `reasoning_content` are not preserved when building `ChatCompletionAssistantMessageParam`.

A narrow fix would be to provide a way for OpenAI-compatible providers to preserve/replay vendor-specific assistant-message fields, at least `reasoning_content`, without sending it for providers that do not support it.

comments.body:
To help triage, here's how this issue fits together with the other reasoning-content reports, and where the gaps are after the DeepSeek RC1 fix and the OpenAI-compatible PR. This issue covers the **send-side** half; the full cluster spans four stages of one pipeline: ```mermaid flowchart TD R["Model response
(reasoning_content / reasoning / <think>)"] S1["① RECEIVE — buildGeneration()
⚠ #6020: field name varies across providers,
not captured on the openai-java path"] S2["② STORE — AssistantMessage
🏗 #5698: unify into a common ThinkingAssistantMessage"] S3["③ MERGE (streaming) — merge() / internalStream()
⚠ streaming axis: reasoning lost during chunk merge"] S4["④ SEND — createRequest(), hardcoded null
⚠ #6016: dropped on replay for OpenAI-compatible providers"] E["💥 HTTP 400 — 'reasoning_content must be passed back'"] R --> S1 --> S2 --> S3 --> S4 --> E ``` **Why it matters:** fixing ④ alone isn't enough — if ① doesn't capture the field there's nothing to replay, and if ③ drops it the streaming path stays broken even after ④ is fixed. **Coverage / gap matrix** | Stage | OpenAI-compatible | Native DeepSeek | Ollama | |---|---|---|---| | ① receive (#6020) | ⚠ gap | native subclass OK | ⚠ gap | | ③ stream merge | — | ❌ gap (no dedicated issue) | — | | ④ send (this issue / #6026) | 🟡 PR #6296 (open) | ✅ fixed in `2.0.0-RC1`; #6189 closed as duplicate of #6143 | ❌ no PR | **In-flight / resolved PRs:** - #6296 — OpenAI-compatible send path (`Closes #6016 (OpenAI path)`) — still open - #6143 — native DeepSeek send path — fixed in `2.0.0-RC1` **Gaps that remain after #6296 lands:** 1. **① receive-side field-name normalization (#6020)** — `reasoning_content` vs `reasoning` vs inline `…`, on the OpenAI-compatible / openai-java path. 2. **③ streaming chunk-merge loss** — currently only noted in #6026's comments (`merge()` / `internalStream()`), no dedicated issue. 3. **④ Ollama send path** — listed in this issue's table but not covered by any PR. **Relation to #5698:** a common `ThinkingAssistantMessage` would collapse ①③④ into a single place; until then every model needs the same read-through duplicated. So #5698 is the architectural superset of this cluster rather than a competing fix.

title: ToolCallAdvisor >= 1.1.3 streamWithToolCallResponses Bug
body: When ToolCallAdvisor is configured in ChatClient, the Flux stream continues to receive a cancel signal after receiving the completion signal. The following code in the streamWithToolCallResponses method of the ToolCallAdvisor class: publish() converts a cold stream into a hot stream. Internally, it creates a ConnectableFlux. If doOnComplete and doOnCancel are used in the Flux stream during the model invocation or in the Flux processing of other custom advisors, the program will receive a doOnCancel signal after executing doOnComplete, thereby triggering the logic inside doOnCancel. logs: 2026-05-13T10:12:49.958+08:00 ERROR 31052 --- [nio-8080-exec-1] com.og.ai.config.model.SuperChatModel : >>> 发生订阅: 0aeae39b72214746a137da75edc7f7a0 thread: http-nio-8080-exec-1 2026-05-13T10:12:52.085+08:00 ERROR 31052 --- [ient-2-Worker-2] com.og.ai.config.model.SuperChatModel : 请求完成: 0aeae39b72214746a137da75edc7f7a0 2026-05-13T10:12:52.086+08:00 ERROR 31052 --- [ient-2-Worker-2] com.og.ai.config.model.SuperChatModel : 请求结束: 0aeae39b72214746a137da75edc7f7a0 onComplete 2026-05-13T10:12:52.160+08:00 ERROR 31052 --- [oundedElastic-1] com.og.ai.config.model.SuperChatModel : 请求被取消: 0aeae39b72214746a137da75edc7f7a0

comments.author: anxinyh
sdeleuze
comments.body: @chemicL Could you please qualify this issue and related PR?

comments.author: chemicL
comments.body:
@anxinyh can you please clarify what consequence do you see with the current code? I do understand you are getting a cancel signal but what does it mean in practice with a particular model/use-case?

As far as I understand:
1. `publish(Function)` is not the same as `publish()` (without arguments) - it is not transforming the upstream to a hot flux, it just shares a single subscription across multiple downstream subscribers. And it does not return a `ConnectableFlux` so that is incorrect in the assessment in this issue.
2. `cancel` post-completion should have no effect according to rule 1.6 of the Reactive Stream specification (https://github.com/reactive-streams/reactive-streams-jvm/blob/v1.0.4/README.md) – the Subscription is considered effectively cancelled. It should also be idempotent according to 3.5. Rule 3.7 even demands that after a Subscription is cancelled it should be [NOP](https://github.com/reactive-streams/reactive-streams-jvm/blob/v1.0.4/README.md#term_nop).

Let's discuss the reason for the report and whether there is a bug somewhere else potentially?

comments.author: jewoodev
comments.body:
Hi, I can take a look at this.

**Quick diagnosis**: 
This looks like a base-URL path change from the `openai-java` SDK migration in M5. In 1.x, Spring AI appended `/v1/chat/completions` via `completionsPath`, so `http://localhost:12434/engines` became `…/engines/v1/chat/completions`. With the new SDK, the client expects the base URL to already include `/v1` and appends only `chat/completions`, so the same config resolves to `…/engines/chat/completions` and returns 404.

**Workaround**:
`spring.ai.openai.chat.base-url=http://localhost:12434/engines/v1`

If using `spring.ai.openai.base-url` instead, the existing `spring.ai.openai.chat.base-url` override should be removed because the chat-specific value takes precedence.

This also looks like a small docs drift: `openai-chat.adoc` still documents `spring.ai.openai.chat.completions-path`, but that property no longer exists after the SDK migration. Happy to send a small focused PR to update the OpenAI chat docs / M5 upgrade notes and add a Docker Model Runner note, unless you prefer restoring a `completions-path`-like escape hatch.

| `dmr-chat.adoc:100` | The documented base URL is `https://hub.docker.com/u/ai`, which is a Docker Hub user page rather than an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint. | `POST https://hub.docker.com/u/ai/chat/completions` returns an HTML body with HTTP 200, not JSON; `.../u/ai/v1/chat/completions` returns 404. |
| `openai-embeddings.adoc:148`, `openai-speech.adoc:93,112`, `openai-transcriptions.adoc:91,112`, `openai-moderation.adoc:87,103` | Four sibling `*-path` properties are still documented even though they were removed with the SDK migration. | The same commit `75fa84486` that removed `completions-path` also removed `embeddings-path`, `speech-path`, `transcription-path`, and `moderation-path`. |
| `dmr-chat.adoc:6,20,125,184,247` | The rest of the Docker Model Runner page still shows `http://localhost:12434/engines`. | The new note in `openai-chat.adoc` recommends `http://localhost:12434/engines/v1`; I could not run Docker Model Runner locally, so I am flagging this as an internal docs inconsistency rather than a verified runtime failure. |
| `ollama-chat.adoc:609` | The OpenAI-compatible Ollama example uses `http://localhost:11434` without `/v1`. | `OllamaWithOpenAiChatModelIT.java:84` uses `http://localhost:11434/v1` as the base URL. |
| `groq-chat.adoc:7,26,36,58,142,168,293,359` | The Groq OpenAI-compatible base URL is documented as `https://api.groq.com/openai`. | `https://api.groq.com/openai/chat/completions` returns 404, while `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions` returns 401 and reaches the auth layer. |

A smaller wording-only point: the new Docker Model Runner note in `openai-chat.adoc` says users "may need" to append `/v1`. comments.author: DragonFSKY
comments.body:
Hi, I looked into this and I think this is a valid issue.

From the current code path, `OpenAiEmbeddingModel` already passes `embeddingRequest.getOptions()` into `OpenAiEmbeddingOptions.Builder.merge(...)`. However, `merge(...)` currently only copies fields when the runtime options are `OpenAiEmbeddingOptions`. When the request uses the generic `EmbeddingOptions.builder()`, common fields such as `model` and `dimensions` are not merged, so the default OpenAI embedding model is still used.

This seems different from some other embedding model implementations, where common `EmbeddingOptions` fields are merged before provider-specific fields.

I would be happy to work on a focused fix for this. My plan would be to merge the common `EmbeddingOptions#getModel()` and `getDimensions()` fields while keeping OpenAI-specific fields, including deployment name semantics, unchanged.

comments.author: DragonFSKY
comments.body:
Thanks for reporting this.

I took a quick look at the code, and I think this might be related to `ChatClient.prompt(Prompt)` not propagating the `ChatOptions` carried by the given `Prompt`. From what I can see, it copies the prompt messages into the request spec, but the prompt-level options, such as `OpenAiChatOptions.model(...)`, are not preserved. That could explain why configuring the model through properties works, while setting the model on the `Prompt` is ignored in this path.

I also checked a bit of the history around this area. Before the options-merging refactoring in #5725 / commit `4b251d19e`, `ChatClient.prompt(Prompt)` did propagate `prompt.getOptions()` into the request spec. That refactoring intentionally moved options merging to the ChatClient level via `ChatOptions.Builder#combineWith(...)`, but I could not find anything indicating that prompt-level options from `Prompt` should now be ignored.

So my current understanding is that this might be a small regression from that refactoring: `ChatClientRequestSpec.options(...)` changed to accept a `ChatOptions.Builder`, but the `Prompt` options path was not carried over with `prompt.getOptions().mutate()`.

Would it make sense to update `ChatClient.prompt(Prompt)` to also carry over `prompt.getOptions()` into the request spec, and add a regression test to verify that prompt-level options are preserved?

I would be happy to contribute a PR if this sounds like the right direction. Please let me know if I missed any intended behavior here.
That sounds like the right direction, a PR would be greatly appreciated!

title: Per-call `customHeaders` not propagated in `OpenAiImageOptions`
body:
**Bug description**

`OpenAiImageOptions#customHeaders` set on a per-`ImagePrompt` basis are never applied to the outgoing OpenAI image request. The map is only consumed once, when the underlying `OpenAIClient` is built in `OpenAiSetup.setupSyncClient(...)`. As a result, headers configured at runtime (per call) are silently dropped.

Use case affected: calling LLM-gateway proxies (e.g. internal cost-attribution gateways) that require a per-request header such as `x-budget-id` derived from the business request. A static client-level header is not sufficient.

This is inconsistent with the chat-side `OpenAiChatOptions`, where per-call `customHeaders` are propagated to the underlying `ChatCompletionCreateParams.additionalHeaders`.

**Environment**

- Spring AI: `main` (verified on commit `2bbd95596`) and `2.0.0-M6`
- Spring Boot: 4.0.6
- openai-java: 4.34.0
- JDK 25

**Steps to reproduce**

```java
ImageResponse resp = openAiImageModel.call(new ImagePrompt(
    "a ducati motorcycle",
    OpenAiImageOptions.builder()
        .model("gpt-image-2")
        .size("1024x1024")
        .quality("medium")
        .customHeaders(Map.of("x-budget-id", "BUDGET_123"))
        .build()));
```

Inspect the outgoing HTTP request (`OPENAI_LOG=debug`). The `x-budget-id` header is **not** present on the `/v1/images/generations` call.

**Expected behavior**

Per-call `customHeaders` should be propagated as `additionalHeaders` on the `ImageGenerateParams` sent to `openAiClient.images().generate(params)`, matching the chat-side semantics.

**Root cause**

`OpenAiImageOptions#toOpenAiImageGenerateParams(ImagePrompt)` builds the `ImageGenerateParams` from typed fields (`n`, `quality`, `size`, `style`, `user`, `responseFormat`, `model`) but never reads `getCustomHeaders()`. See `models/spring-ai-openai/src/main/java/org/springframework/ai/openai/OpenAiImageOptions.java` (the `toOpenAiImageGenerateParams` method).

**Minimal Complete Reproducible example**

Failing test (passes after the fix):

```java
@Test
void customHeadersPropagatedToImageGenerateParams() {
    var options = OpenAiImageOptions.builder()
        .model("gpt-image-1")
        .customHeaders(Map.of("x-budget-id", "BUDGET_123"))
        .build();

    var prompt = new ImagePrompt("a ducati motorcycle", options);
    var params = options.toOpenAiImageGenerateParams(prompt);

    assertThat(params._additionalHeaders().values("x-budget-id"))
        .containsExactly("BUDGET_123");
}
```

title: Exclude `jackson-dataformat-yaml` from `json-schema-validator`
body:
**Bug description**
The `org.springframework.ai:spring-ai-client-chat` uses `com.networknt:json-schema-validator` for the `StructuredOutputValidationAdvisor` to perform schema validation. This was done in https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-ai/pull/5773 to remove the `mcp-json-jackson3` dependency.

**Environment**
Spring AI 2.0.0-M6

**Steps to reproduce**

Add the `org.springframework.ai:spring-ai-client-chat` dependency to an empty Spring Boot project. And among the dependency tree there is:

```
+- com.networknt:json-schema-validator:jar:3.0.1:compile
|  +- com.ethlo.time:itu:jar:1.14.0:compile
|  +- tools.jackson.dataformat:jackson-dataformat-yaml:jar:3.1.2:compile
|  |  \- org.snakeyaml:snakeyaml-engine:jar:3.0.1:compile
|  \- org.slf4j:slf4j-api:jar:2.0.17:compile
```

**Expected behavior**

I would expect dependencies like this to be optional in Spring AI. The `StructuredOutputValidationAdvisor` is not used anywhere else in Spring AI itself, it's only there for users to use it if they want to. Perhaps the auto configuration / starter dependencies could pull the dependency. However, I think it's a bit too much to pull so much just for the potentially someone using the validation advisor.

Pulling the `jackson-dataformat-yaml` also means that all REST Endpoints by default with Spring Boot are going to accept YAML as input and / or the `WebClient` / `RestClient` are going to advertise that they accept `application/yaml` as response.

comments.author: sdeleuze
comments.body: @filiphr Could you please create a related issue on https://github.com/networknt/json-schema-validator asking them to make Yaml support optional? I would like to see if they could fix that at the source since they already have a few optional dependencies.

comments.author: ThomasVitale
comments.body:
Similar to other optional advisors like vector store, RAG, and tool search, it could be an idea to move StructuredOutputValidationAdvisor and related dependencies to a dedicated module that users can include in their projects if they need to. 

Most inference services these days support native structured outputs. The advisor would not be needed in those cases. When using models without native structured outputs support, it would be possible to add the explicit module in the project to use the validator advisor.

title: `tool` role messages sent without preceding `tool_calls` after Azure→OpenAI module consolidation
body:
### Spring AI Version
`2.0.0-SNAPSHOT` (post Azure module consolidation)

### Description

After upgrading from Spring AI 1.x (with `spring-ai-azure-openai`) to the Spring AI 2.0 snapshot (which consolidates Azure support into `spring-ai-openai`), a previously working application now throws a `400 Bad Request` from the OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```
com.openai.errors.BadRequestException: 400: Invalid parameter: messages with role 'tool' must be a response to a preceeding message with 'tool_calls'.
```

The error originates in `OpenAiChatModel.internalCall` and propagates through the advisor chain (`ChatModelCallAdvisor` → `BaseAdvisor` → `DefaultAroundAdvisorChain`).

### Stack Trace

```
com.openai.errors.BadRequestException: 400: Invalid parameter: messages with role 'tool' must be a response to a preceeding message with 'tool_calls'.
    at com.openai.errors.BadRequestException$Builder.build(BadRequestException.kt:98)
    at com.openai.core.handlers.ErrorHandler$errorHandler$1.handle(ErrorHandler.kt:54)
    at com.openai.services.blocking.chat.ChatCompletionServiceImpl$WithRawResponseImpl.create(ChatCompletionServiceImpl.kt:141)
    at org.springframework.ai.openai.OpenAiChatModel.lambda$internalCall$4(OpenAiChatModel.java:212)
    at org.springframework.ai.openai.OpenAiChatModel.internalCall(OpenAiChatModel.java:210)
    at org.springframework.ai.openai.OpenAiChatModel.call(OpenAiChatModel.java:189)
    at org.springframework.ai.chat.client.advisor.ChatModelCallAdvisor.adviseCall(ChatModelCallAdvisor.java:58)
    at org.springframework.ai.chat.client.advisor.DefaultAroundAdvisorChain.lambda$nextCall$1(DefaultAroundAdvisorChain.java:115)
    at org.springframework.ai.chat.client.advisor.DefaultAroundAdvisorChain.nextCall(DefaultAroundAdvisorChain.java:114)
    at org.springframework.ai.chat.client.advisor.api.BaseAdvisor.adviseCall(BaseAdvisor.java:52)
    at org.springframework.ai.chat.client.advisor.DefaultAroundAdvisorChain.lambda$nextCall$1(DefaultAroundAdvisorChain.java:115)
    at org.springframework.ai.chat.client.advisor.DefaultAroundAdvisorChain.nextCall(DefaultAroundAdvisorChain.java:114)
```

### Root Cause (Hypothesis)

The `spring-ai-azure-openai` module previously handled tool call message assembly using Azure OpenAI SDK conventions. With the consolidation into `spring-ai-openai`, the new module uses the `com.openai` Java SDK (`OpenAiChatModel`), which enforces strict OpenAI message ordering: a `role: tool` message **must** immediately follow an assistant message containing `tool_calls`.

The suspicion is that when conversation history is rehydrated (e.g., from `ChatMemory` / Redis), or when `ToolCallAdvisor` reconstructs the message list for a subsequent tool call round, one or more `TOOL` role messages are being inserted into the prompt without a corresponding preceding `ASSISTANT` message that contains `tool_calls`. This could be caused by:

- Conversation history serialization/deserialization dropping the `tool_calls` metadata from assistant messages
- The message list builder in `OpenAiChatModel` or its request mapper not preserving the `tool_calls` field on assistant messages loaded from memory
- `ToolCallAdvisor` reconstructing history in a way that was tolerated by the Azure SDK but is rejected by the stricter `com.openai` SDK validation

### To Reproduce

1. Configure a Spring AI 2.0 snapshot application using `spring-ai-openai` pointing at an Azure OpenAI endpoint
2. Use `ToolCallAdvisor` (or `BoundedToolCallAdvisor`) with at least one `@Tool`-annotated method
3. Persist conversation history across turns using `ChatMemory` (e.g., `JdbcChatMemoryRepository`)
4. Invoke a tool call in one turn, then send a follow-up message in the next turn
5. Observe the `400 Bad Request` on the second (or subsequent) call

### Expected Behavior

The message list sent to the OpenAI endpoint should preserve the `assistant` message (with `tool_calls`) immediately before any `tool` result message(s), matching the protocol requirement. This worked correctly with the legacy `spring-ai-azure-openai` module.

### Actual Behavior

A `400 Bad Request` is returned because a `role: tool` message appears in the request without a preceding `role: assistant` message containing `tool_calls`.

### Environment

- Spring AI: `2.0.0-SNAPSHOT` (post Azure consolidation)
- Spring Boot: `4.0.x`
- Azure OpenAI endpoint (accessed via `spring-ai-openai` with custom base URL)
- Java 25

### Additional Context

This regression is specific to the `com.openai` SDK-backed `OpenAiChatModel` introduced in 2.0. The legacy `azure-openai` module used a different request-building path that was apparently more lenient about message ordering, or correctly preserved the `tool_calls` field on serialized/deserialized assistant messages. The fix likely needs to ensure that wherever assistant messages containing tool invocations are stored and reloaded, their `tool_calls` payload is preserved through the full serialization roundtrip.

title: 2.0.0-M7 forces API key requirement, breaking cookie/session-based authentication
body:
### **Bug description**

**Spring Boot Version:** 4.0.2
**Spring AI Version:** 2.0.0-M7
**Java Version:** 25

### **Problem Summary**
Spring AI 2.0.0-M7 introduces a breaking change that requires an API key credential at client construction time, making it impossible to use cookie/session-based authentication with custom/internal AI servers.

### **Expected Behavior**
In Spring AI 1.0.0-M6, I could create an `OpenAiChatModel` without providing a valid API key, allowing my custom authentication (cookies) to handle all security. The framework would not force an `Authorization` header.

### **Actual Behavior**
- **Without any API key:** Client fails to build with error: `"At least one credential source must be specified: credential (apiKey), workloadIdentity, or adminApiKey"`
- **With dummy API key:** Client builds successfully BUT forces `Authorization: Bearer dummy` header on every request, causing my server to reject with `403 PermissionDenied` or `404 Not Found`

### **Authentication Flow (Working with 1.0.0-M6)**
```bash
# 1. Login to get session cookie
curl --request POST https://my-ai-server/app_login \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"login": "service_account", "password": "secret"}' \
  --cookie-jar cookies.txt

# 2. Use cookie for AI requests (NO API key needed)
curl --request POST https://my-ai-server/v1/chat/completions \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"model": "my-model", "messages": [...]}' \
  --cookie cookies.txt 
```

In 1.0.0-M6 I had manually created RestClient and WebClient for handling cookies and NoopApiKey().

Root Cause Analysis
The underlying OpenAI Java SDK requires one of three credential types (apiKey, workloadIdentity, or adminApiKey) to be set. In 1.0.0-M6, Spring AI provided a NoopApiKey that bypassed the Authorization header. In 2.0.0-M7, this mechanism appears to have been removed or changed, forcing the header to be sent.

Workarounds Attempted (None successful)
❌ Setting spring.ai.openai.chat.enabled=false - Does not work (auto-config still validates)
❌ Setting all spring.ai.model.*=none - Does not work (validation happens at client level)
❌ Using WorkloadIdentity with dummy token provider - Still sends authentication header
❌ Custom Credential implementation - The Credential interface is empty, implementation unclear
❌ HTTP interceptor with reflection - Possible but fragile (requires internal API access, not production-ready)

Could the Spring AI team please:
- Restore the NoopApiKey functionality, OR
- Provide an official way to disable the Authorization header for cookie/session-based authentication scenarios

This is a production-blocking issue as we are migrating to Spring Boot 4.0.2 and cannot use older Spring AI versions, while our AI server requires cookie-only authentication.

title: Remove toolNames() API and SpringBeanToolCallbackResolver — use explicit ToolCallback beans instead
body:
### Problem

Spring AI currently supports resolving of java.util.Function tools by Spring bean name via `SpringBeanToolCallbackResolver` and `toolNames()`:

```java
@Bean
@Description("Get the weather in location")
public Function<Request, Response> weatherFunction() { ... }

chatClient.prompt()
    .toolNames("weatherFunction")  // untyped string reference
    .call();
```
This pattern is inconsistent with Spring AI's other tool definition approaches and has several drawbacks:

- Untyped, runtime-only binding — renaming or removing the bean breaks at runtime, not compile time
- Scattered tool definition — description and input type are split across the bean declaration and call site
- Inconsistent API — requires dedicated toolNames() / defaultToolNames() methods on every options builder solely to support this one pattern
- Implicit application context coupling — tool resolution depends on bean naming, scope, and context visibility

### Solution

Remove `SpringBeanToolCallbackResolver` and all `toolNames()` / `defaultToolNames()` methods. Users should declare tools explicitly using one of the existing approaches:

```java
ToolCallback weatherFunction =  FunctionToolCallback.builder("weatherFunction", new MockWeatherService())
        .description("Get the weather in location")
        .inputType(Request.class)
        .build();
```

### Scope

- Delete SpringBeanToolCallbackResolver
- Remove toolNames() / defaultToolNames() from ChatClient, ChatClient.Builder, and all model-specific options builders
- Remove spring.ai.*.chat.tool-names auto-configuration properties

#### Affected Issues to be removed
Based on the search results, these 4 open issues would be closed/resolved as obsolete by this change since they report bugs in a feature that would no longer exist:

#2399 — "SpringBeanToolCallbackResolver has a problem with bean cache inside"
#2617 — "The generateSchema function of SpringBeanToolCallbackResolver works as not expected"
#2632 — "Using @Tool annotation for Function beans?"
#2667 — "springBeanToolCallbackResolver want to create a bean which is not existed"
You could reference them in the new issue with Closes #2399, Closes #2617, Closes #2632, Closes #2667 so they auto-close when the PR merges.
